before.title: AmberX: slim down + voice queue
before.detail:
1) Voice queue: AmberX holds everything Brett says; nothing sent to Claude until he says "process", then sends the whole batch in one turn (save tokens).
2) Scrap the bloat. AmberX keeps ONLY: to-do, notes, task manager, session recorder, screen recording, Gizmo chat (agent chat). Remove/disable everything else.

before.title: Approve / deny axHub approvals inside the Dev Console (no bounce to axHub)
before.detail: Tapping an approval in the console opened axHub. Now: the console server relays Brett's own hub session (axhub_session cookie on .amberxai.com, wall-signed admin, same-origin tap) to axHub's decide API (session + CSRF + hub Origin), so the banner, app-menu rows, review dialog, Follow Amber pop-up and console_show approval:<id> decide in place with the result shown. Review dialog = in-console approval view (title, description, exact call, countdown, Approve/Deny, result), axHub link only secondary. Console actions approvals.approve/deny/view. AmberX notification taps open the console view.

notes.text: Reconciler: paused: no live session or process runs it (worktree kept); was running

origin.said: It does pop it up in my approval, but when I click it, it brings me to axHub. I don't want it to bring me to axHub.

before.title: Token usage log + accounts + Plan Studio control
before.detail: From plan token-usage-log-rules-briefs-api-run-approvals-3gcg (Brett, voice, Nov 6 2026): its 11 steps plus every add-on.

steps.text: Token log NOW: every headless session logs per turn input/output/cache tokens, cost, model, account, build/step, session, files read (flag CLAUDE.md/rules reads), from transcripts; plain code on VPS, zero tokens
Chat/voice sessions log what they can (tool calls, estimates via session notes / synced chats), marked estimated
Claude settings > Token log viewer: per session/account/build/model, top token eaters, filters, totals by day
Every API-key run is a confirm approval (never veto): dialog with estimated cost before, final cost after
Persist the API-run approval rule in _claude/shared/rules/RULES.md + decisions.md (via PR)
Periodic cheap headless check reads logs + synced chats (no CLAUDE.md) and tallies usage
Headless sessions skip CLAUDE.md/rules files; get orchestrator task brief + a rules brief (short digest). Update load-rules-first rule to exempt headless
Claude settings > Rules briefs: editor, multiple saved briefs, conditions for when each runs, option to generate on the fly before send
Orchestrator task brief shown read-only next to the rules brief; both sent together on launch
Every completed step auto-ticked in the plan and to-do manager (synced)
Completed steps: multi-select + button to split into their own PR; default merge queue, optional 'go live right away'

Full control of Plan Studio through the API, CLI and MCP: everything the UI can do (create, rename, edit fields, status, priority, add/edit/remove/reorder steps, merge and delete plans, turn into builds)
Widgets and the banner: option to show icon only
Every plan that will become a build gets an orchestrator build ID as soon as it is created, so steps sync and show in Plan Studio
Every build, wherever it comes from, goes through the orchestrator first: it registers it, assigns IDs and dispatches it
Account switch actually signs the VPS Claude login in to the active account
Save the rotated refresh token after every login/renew
Banner clock badge watches the VPS login live: green connected, yellow out of tokens, red not connected
Per-account usage meter in each row of the account picker plugin (used out of total)
Banner widget, hidden by default, showing the usage meter of the account signed in on the VPS
On every VPS account connect, a separate headless session tests all other accounts' usage and updates the accounts grid
Running builds follow the active account; auto failover to the subscription account with the most remaining credits; API keys always last; any switch to API usage needs an approval, never a veto
Approve in the console pop-up never opens new windows
Veto notices only for VPS writes and Claude account switches
Brett's admin console login counts as owner for owner-only Claude settings
'Start a build plan' = parked Plan Studio plan; each thing Brett adds is a step shown in Plan Studio
Tap Parked opens a dialog: Cancel, Delete, Send to orchestrator
Any step list: multi-select + right-click to remove, add to an existing build, or make a new build (send now or park)
Plan steps show as a checklist like the to-do manager; expand plan = grid of steps, expand step = details, multi-select
Plans sync with the to-do manager only once launched as a build, not while parked
All syncing runs as plain code on the VPS, zero Claude tokens

after.title: Memory restructure: chunked CLAUDE.md store + Memory Manager plugin
after.detail: Fresh memory bank for amberx-axf. 1) Split _claude/handoff/context/CLAUDE.md (~240 KB) and everything it chains to (@ imports, THREADS.md, STATUS.md, decisions.md, memory/docs) into a chunked storage file in the repo: one chunk per Status entry/section plus a short index (one line per chunk) so sessions load only the pieces they need. 2) New CLAUDE.md stays tiny: at session start it asks the orchestrator what to load; the orchestrator reports only builds started in the last 24 h that stopped unfinished. Builds data belongs to the orchestrator, not Claude memory. 3) Delete the whole handoff part of the console (_claude/handoff + claude-handoff plugin writers); Brett restarts it later. 4) Audit every part of the app that writes to memory (THREADS.md, sessions/, builds/reports, handoff, STATUS.md, etc.) and list them. 5) Build a Memory Manager console plugin: duplicate (do not share) MD Studio's code so MD Studio can be deleted later; scan/refresh to find every memory file, show what reads and what writes each one, and full management (view, edit, move, delete, versions).

before.title: Headless progress file + lean CLAUDE.md chain
before.detail: Every headless build session writes progress to a small status file in the build and never stops to update the console; console reads it when needed. Also make headless sessions efficient with the CLAUDE.md chain (Brett, voice, Nov 6 2026).

notes.text: Reconciler: paused: no live session or process runs it (worktree kept); was running

before.title: Planner: select items and build them
before.detail: In Plan Studio, select any parts (single steps or features at any depth, or the whole plan) with multi-select, then click Create build to make one build from the selection.

notes.text: Brett: "Without AI." Select and create build must work with no AI: plain UI that assembles the brief from the selected items directly.

Brett: "So whenever you plan something, it gets a file that writes out what it would prompt AI to say. What it would tell you, but it doesn't say anything until you, unless you add it to a new build." Every plan item has a stored, prewritten prompt file. Nothing is sent to AI until the selection is added to a new build, and then those prompts make up the brief.

Brett: "You can view that file through hooks, the theater. The different steps, maybe the context menu. Or you can do multiple selection, make them rebuild and view the prompt that it generates. Without AI." The prompt file can be viewed per step (theater/hover view, context menu). Multi-select, then rebuild or preview the generated prompt before sending. All of it without AI.

Brett: progress tracking applies to ALL builds, not only ones started from the planner (builds already split into steps). Every build_start brief includes the check-off instruction, and the console reads the progress live for every build. Resume from the first unchecked step.

Re-added (lost in an overwrite): (a) AmberX task and checklist rows: click a row to see the text discussed; expandable rows show amendments; send a row straight to its own new build. (b) A build from the planner auto-ticks items as it finishes them; the brief lists the item IDs and tells it to tick them. (c) The console tracks progress live without AI, through the console API or a progress file in the build dir; no stopping or resending context; if a build dies, the next run resumes at the first unchecked item.

CORRECTION from Brett: the build manager already tracks build progress, so drop the console-tracking and progress-file notes above. NEW: every build (anything Amber or anyone starts) automatically creates a plan in Plan Studio and goes into a build registry. That plan uses the same steps the build manager will use, so they stay in sync (one source of truth) and tick off together, along with the linked AmberX checklist rows. Registry and planner are categorized by app, plugin, edit, feature, in collapsible trees with sorting and filters.
Brett: the build manager and the planner both read and write progress in the SAME registry, one source of truth, with no separate copies to sync.

Brett: backfill the registry: import every existing build (the 79 finished-but-not-landed, the running/queued ones, and landed ones, going back as far as the history goes) as plans with their steps and status, read from the build dirs, briefs, logs, and git branches.
Brett: each registry/plan entry shows its addenda and amendments: every later change, note, or restart (e.g. r2/r3 runs), in order with timestamps, in expandable rows. Backfill them too.

after.title: FIRST: Refresh token saved every time it's used (VPS Claude login)
after.detail: Top priority, build before anything else (one build at a time). Every time the VPS Claude login (MossesX) or any saved account renews or uses its refresh token, the rotated refresh + access token are written back at once to the saved copy (ai-keys store and /root/.claude-accounts) so the next run never uses a dead token. Covers headless claude -p launches, ai-keys renew thread, and account switches. Also: save the current VPS login (MossesX, after Brett signs in) under its own name so switching never overwrites it; let the console delete VPS-folder accounts (delete route currently says 'no such key' for vps:* accounts). Tests with fake tokens. Same as step 17 of token-usage-log-accounts-plan-studio-control and step 4 of running-builds-follow-the-active-claude-account: tick those when this lands.

before.title: FIRST: Refresh token saved every time it's used (VPS Claude login)
before.detail: Top priority, build before anything else (one build at a time). Every time the VPS Claude login (MossesX) or any saved account renews or uses its refresh token, the rotated refresh + access token are written back at once to the saved copy (ai-keys store and /root/.claude-accounts) so the next run never uses a dead token. Covers headless claude -p launches, ai-keys renew thread, and account switches. Also: save the current VPS login (MossesX, after Brett signs in) under its own name so switching never overwrites it; let the console delete VPS-folder accounts (delete route currently says 'no such key' for vps:* accounts). Tests with fake tokens. Same as step 17 of token-usage-log-accounts-plan-studio-control and step 4 of running-builds-follow-the-active-claude-account: tick those when this lands.

before.title: FIRST: Refresh token saved every time it's used (VPS Claude login)
before.detail: Top priority, build before anything else (one build at a time). Every time the VPS Claude login (MossesX) or any saved account renews or uses its refresh token, the rotated refresh + access token are written back at once to the saved copy (ai-keys store and /root/.claude-accounts) so the next run never uses a dead token. Covers headless claude -p launches, ai-keys renew thread, and account switches. Also: save the current VPS login (MossesX, after Brett signs in) under its own name so switching never overwrites it; let the console delete VPS-folder accounts (delete route currently says 'no such key' for vps:* accounts). Tests with fake tokens. Same as step 17 of token-usage-log-accounts-plan-studio-control and step 4 of running-builds-follow-the-active-claude-account: tick those when this lands.

before.title: Gizmo: full Claude companion plugin in AmberX
before.detail:
## What Brett said (verbatim, Nov 3 2026, voice)
"I need a companion assistant... a sidekick that allows me to chat to your partner... put the plug-in in AmberX." "A full all-out Claude companion, as full, powerful, as complete as the Claude app itself, with everything, all the features, every setting, the connectors, plugins, a full Claude suite." "We can harvest the assistant code out in AmberX to build the new plugin." "Build the plugin for Claude in AmberX, but make it full, complete. It's gotta be powerful."

Booked to agent Gizmo (all-rounder, $8.00/h, AmberX guide/assistant; replaces agent Molly).

Decisions: lives in AmberX (apps/amberx-droid) as a plugin; harvest AmberX assistant code + console Terminal Claude session code into a shared framework lib (claude-session) + AmberX plugin `companion`; console Terminal keeps working on the shared lib; brains run on the VPS as Claude Code sessions reached through axHub, no API keys in the APK; Gizmo is the face, Molly is no longer an agent.

notes.text: Assigned: Gizmo (headless Opus session, worktree /root/axf-builds/gizmo-companion, branch claude/gizmo-companion)

s10 (s4b) half done: tool calls show as collapsible cards; Follow Amber / console_show hooks not built. s2d: brains are the console AI assistant as agent Gizmo through AmberX's server (no new server code needed).

s9 Gizmo agent card; Molly -> Gizmo in AmberX assistant texts

before.title: Claude settings: tabs, views, Approvals & veto tab

origin.said: "The Claude settings interface is getting pretty big. We need to organize it. Give it multiple views, one of them being tabular. # Build: claude-settings-tabs-veto

## Brett said (verbatim)
"The Claude settings interface is getting pretty big. We need to organize it. Give it multiple views, one of them being tabular. If you have it on the tab view, you can set where you want them to appear and how you want them to appear: on the left, on the right, on the top, and the bottom, whether you want the words or an icon." "The veto and the approve are gonna be their own tab in there. Break it down and put it into tabs."
Also: "You don't need to run the 90-second veto thing unless you are writing stuff to the VPS."

1. Audit Claude settings (plugin claude-settings): list every setting, group them into sensible tabs. Report the breakdown.
2. Views: classic (one page, collapsible sections) and tabbed. Tabbed uses the tab-group@1 asset: tab position left / right / top / bottom, labels as words / icons / both. Settings for the view saved per device. Claude settings stays a settings-interface asset.
3. New tab 'Approvals & veto': per axHub tool (or group) choose allow / veto / confirm, veto hold length (seconds), pass durations; reads go without a hold, only VPS writes and account switches hold by default. Writes to the axHub policy through its API (owner-only). Show the current policy table live.
4. REST/MCP/CLI for the view settings and the policy tab.
5. Tests, README, report, screenshots to UI Review, PR to the merge queue. Do NOT land directly. Overlap check with pending item approvals-no-window-spam-on-approve-veto-only-for-vps-writes-and-account-switc; tick its veto step if covered, note it.

One session, lean chain. Stay out of Gizmo, UI registry, badges/notifications code (other builds).

"Those settings should not be part of the Claude plugin. They can be accessed by any MCP server, the API or the CLI. They can be in Claude settings, they can be in framework settings."
- The approvals/veto policy settings are their own framework-level settings asset (settings-ui@1), owned by the framework, not the claude-settings plugin. Store: framework settings. Exposed on REST + MCP + CLI.
- Mounted in two places as the same asset: Framework settings and a tab in Claude settings. One source of truth.

"Give me a bunch of options in UI Review to pick from, like ten."
- BEFORE building the UI: submit 10 predicted screenshots (ui-review-predicted) of where/how Framework settings and the Approvals & veto settings sit in the main settings interface: e.g. own top-level Framework tab; a section inside General; a left-rail group; a settings home card; a gear in the banner; icon tabs top/left/right/bottom variants; a compact phone layout; a two-pane layout. Phone + desktop each.
- Wait for Brett's pick in UI Review, then build that one. The 10 are mockups only, no code written for the losers.

## Addendum 1 (Brett, voice)
"I need a really sweet interface for the scheduling stuff, the schedules. Make it sick."
- Polished, modern calendar UI (framework tokens + theme only): smooth view transitions, drag to create / move / resize events, colour-coded calendars, now-line, mini-month, quick-add bar (plain English: 'gym every Mon Wed 6pm'), weekly schedule editor with drag blocks, phone gestures (swipe days/weeks, long-press drag), dark/light. Phone-first, desktop great too.
- Screenshots of every view (phone + desktop) to UI Review.

## Addendum 2 (Brett, voice)
"Open that in its own window with multiple layouts. Open numerous schedules, days and weeks: a week here and a month there, and drag events from here to there. Attach an RSVP list / invite list to an event with a check mark of who's replied. Send automatic emails to RSVP people, or emails asking people to confirm they've read/seen it. It needs to update in the scheduler on AmberX."
- Calendar opens in its own window (windows@1 / dock@1); multiple panes side by side, each any view/date/calendar; save named layouts; drag events between panes.
- Invite / RSVP list per event: guests, status (invited / yes / no / maybe / seen), check marks, counts. Emails sent through axHub Google (Gmail) when it exists: invites, automatic RSVP reminders, read/seen confirmation requests (tracked link). Replies update the event status live on console and AmberX. Sending email = confirm approval (axHub policy).

## Addendum 3 (Brett, voice)
"Any replies to the emails get logged. They type their reply in a text field that's sent in the email; they have to reply in the text field so it gets logged in the system."
- Each invite/reminder email has a link to a small public reply page (per-guest signed token, no login): RSVP buttons + a text field. Submissions are logged on the event (who, when, answer, message) and update status live on console + AmberX.
- Plain email replies are also caught via Gmail (axHub) and logged on the event when possible, but the reply page is the main path.
- Reply page is rate-limited, token expires, no other data exposed.

origin.brief:
# today: approve/deny axHub approvals inside the Dev Console

Brett's words (voice, Nov 6 2026): "It does pop it up in my approval, but when I click it, it brings me to axHub. I don't want it to bring me to axHub."

## Problem
When an axHub approval (confirm or veto countdown) is waiting, the console pops it up (approvals-banner / approval popup), but tapping it navigates to https://axhub.amberxai.com/auth/admin/approvals/<id>. Brett wants to stay in the console.

## Build
1. In the console's approval popup/banner (and any approval row in the console, incl. phone layout), tapping the approval opens an in-console approval view: title, description, the exact call/command, countdown if veto, and Approve / Deny buttons.
2. Approve / Deny call axHub's approval API server-side from the console (console proxy using its existing axHub auth), never by sending Brett to the axHub site. Show the result in place (approved, denied, ran, failed).
3. No link to the axHub page as the default tap. At most a small secondary "open in axHub" option.
4. Register console actions (e.g. approvals.approve / approvals.deny with id) so they work through console commands too, and make console_show approval:<id> open this in-console view.
5. AmberX phone notifications for approvals should open the console's in-console view, not axHub.

## Rules
Follow CLAUDE.md and _claude/rules/RULES.md. Never print or log secrets/tokens. Tests for approve/deny from the console. Update help/docs, THREADS row, orchestrator entry, report. Don't land; leave it for Brett's go.

Make UI Review have a separate tab under each one for anything that requires a choice. You need to be able to select multiple with priorities. If you select multiple, it will create a separate view for each one you selected, with the first one being default.

Not all asset types can have more than one view; a settings interface may not need more than one. But make every choice, even the ones I don't pick, an asset, stored in that plugin's folder as an asset for the library.
Every UI in the Appearance section will allow you to choose from any of the assets that have been made for it.

Everything comes shipped (all options as assets). For UI Review, for everything sent through it, I need a minimum of three choices. A setting for the default number of choices, and an option to enable a prompt any time something is sent, asking me how many options I want built.

origin.brief:
# today: approve/deny axHub approvals inside the Dev Console

Brett's words (voice, Nov 6 2026): "It does pop it up in my approval, but when I click it, it brings me to axHub. I don't want it to bring me to axHub."

## Problem
When an axHub approval (confirm or veto countdown) is waiting, the console pops it up (approvals-banner / approval popup), but tapping it navigates to https://axhub.amberxai.com/auth/admin/approvals/<id>. Brett wants to stay in the console.

## Build
1. In the console's approval popup/banner (and any approval row in the console, incl. phone layout), tapping the approval opens an in-console approval view: title, description, the exact call/command, countdown if veto, and Approve / Deny buttons.
2. Approve / Deny call axHub's approval API server-side from the console (console proxy using its existing axHub auth), never by sending Brett to the axHub site. Show the result in place (approved, denied, ran, failed).
3. No link to the axHub page as the default tap. At most a small secondary "open in axHub" option.
4. Register console actions (e.g. approvals.approve / approvals.deny with id) so they work through console commands too, and make console_show approval:<id> open this in-console view.
5. AmberX phone notifications for approvals should open the console's in-console view, not axHub.

## Rules
Follow CLAUDE.md and _claude/rules/RULES.md. Never print or log secrets/tokens. Tests for approve/deny from the console. Update help/docs, THREADS row, orchestrator entry, report. Don't land; leave it for Brett's go.

Make UI Review have a separate tab under each one for anything that requires a choice. You need to be able to select multiple with priorities. If you select multiple, it will create a separate view for each one you selected, with the first one being default.

Not all asset types can have more than one view; a settings interface may not need more than one. But make every choice, even the ones I don't pick, an asset, stored in that plugin's folder as an asset for the library.
Every UI in the Appearance section will allow you to choose from any of the assets that have been made for it.

Everything comes shipped (all options as assets). For UI Review, for everything sent through it, I need a minimum of three choices. A setting for the default number of choices, and an option to enable a prompt any time something is sent, asking me how many options I want built.

origin.said: "We're gonna build a UI asset designer, which will create assets with their manifest and their identifier. It's going to create separate plugins for the app menu designer, the nav menu designer, the toolbar designer, the banner designer, the embedded widget designer, the widget designer. These are not dependent on the designer, but the designer interface will inherit those other designers. The UI designer plugin will have add-ons, each with their own settings interface and the designer's interface." "Redo them all from scratch." "Make it a build and get the Fable stuff going. Make it super powerful: full-blown context menu, drag and drop, map-based. Every UI asset will also have a context menu section which gives you a preview of the UI, and informs you in multiple ways (tooltips etc)."

steps.text: designer@1 contract: host + add-on model (designer-addon@1: id, asset types, designer UI view, settings interface asset, designer interface asset, manifest fields, capabilities, drops, voice), the designer asset type (the designer's interface with inherit@1 copies per add-on), rules file + .d.mts, exported from core

Asset output contract: designed@1 manifest + stable identifier (uid, ref, revision, hash, origin), registration as a ui-registry@1 item (coordinated with ui-registry-shortcuts, no duplicate engine) and in the designer library index (designer-library@1, paths per output target); the embed asset type (embed-asset@1)

Interaction contract for every designer (designer-doc@1): one document model with families per asset type (toolbar, banner, nav, app menu, context menu, flat) and asset round trips, ops, multi-select, map canvas (snap, align, distribute, auto layout, zoom), drag-and-drop (parseDrop / canDrop / applyDrop), undo / redo with coalescing, the designer context menu + keyboard map

asset-context@1: the context-menu section every UI asset gets (identity with tooltip, live Preview entry, About, Help, Edit in its designer, Copy id, Where used) and assetInfo in every mode (tooltip, hover card, side panel, help text, say); MenuEntry gains tip / preview / disabled; data-axf-asset attribute contract

Fixtures + validators + checks: spec/fixtures/designer.json replayed by spec/check-designer.mjs (CI), both validators agree, starters (designer ×7, settings ×7, embed ×3), JSON Schemas, re-bake + shared-assets bake, PORTING.md row, DESIGNER.md spec, report, Opus steps written into the plan
PR into the merge queue (never landed directly), THREADS.md + STATUS.md + decisions.md, build linked (builds-live.mjs link)

origin.said: "We're gonna build a UI asset designer, which will create assets with their manifest and their identifier. It's going to create separate plugins for the app menu designer, the nav menu designer, the toolbar designer, the banner designer, the embedded widget designer, the widget designer. These are not dependent on the designer, but the designer interface will inherit those other designers. The UI designer plugin will have add-ons, each with their own settings interface and the designer's interface." "Redo them all from scratch." "Make it a build and get the Fable stuff going. Make it super powerful: full-blown context menu, drag and drop, map-based. Every UI asset will also have a context menu section which gives you a preview of the UI, and informs you in multiple ways (tooltips etc)."

steps.text: designer@1 contract: host + add-on model (designer-addon@1: id, asset types, designer UI view, settings interface asset, designer interface asset, manifest fields, capabilities, drops, voice), the designer asset type (the designer's interface with inherit@1 copies per add-on), rules file + .d.mts, exported from core

Asset output contract: designed@1 manifest + stable identifier (uid, ref, revision, hash, origin), registration as a ui-registry@1 item (coordinated with ui-registry-shortcuts, no duplicate engine) and in the designer library index (designer-library@1, paths per output target); the embed asset type (embed-asset@1)

Interaction contract for every designer (designer-doc@1): one document model with families per asset type (toolbar, banner, nav, app menu, context menu, flat) and asset round trips, ops, multi-select, map canvas (snap, align, distribute, auto layout, zoom), drag-and-drop (parseDrop / canDrop / applyDrop), undo / redo with coalescing, the designer context menu + keyboard map

asset-context@1: the context-menu section every UI asset gets (identity with tooltip, live Preview entry, About, Help, Edit in its designer, Copy id, Where used) and assetInfo in every mode (tooltip, hover card, side panel, help text, say); MenuEntry gains tip / preview / disabled; data-axf-asset attribute contract

Fixtures + validators + checks: spec/fixtures/designer.json replayed by spec/check-designer.mjs (CI), both validators agree, starters (designer ×7, settings ×7, embed ×3), JSON Schemas, re-bake + shared-assets bake, PORTING.md row, DESIGNER.md spec, report, Opus steps written into the plan
PR into the merge queue (never landed directly), THREADS.md + STATUS.md + decisions.md, build linked (builds-live.mjs link)

origin.said: "We're gonna build a UI asset designer, which will create assets with their manifest and their identifier. It's going to create separate plugins for the app menu designer, the nav menu designer, the toolbar designer, the banner designer, the embedded widget designer, the widget designer. These are not dependent on the designer, but the designer interface will inherit those other designers. The UI designer plugin will have add-ons, each with their own settings interface and the designer's interface." "Redo them all from scratch." "Make it a build and get the Fable stuff going. Make it super powerful: full-blown context menu, drag and drop, map-based. Every UI asset will also have a context menu section which gives you a preview of the UI, and informs you in multiple ways (tooltips etc)."

steps.text: designer@1 contract: host + add-on model (designer-addon@1: id, asset types, designer UI view, settings interface asset, designer interface asset, manifest fields, capabilities, drops, voice), the designer asset type (the designer's interface with inherit@1 copies per add-on), rules file + .d.mts, exported from core

Asset output contract: designed@1 manifest + stable identifier (uid, ref, revision, hash, origin), registration as a ui-registry@1 item (coordinated with ui-registry-shortcuts, no duplicate engine) and in the designer library index (designer-library@1, paths per output target); the embed asset type (embed-asset@1)

Interaction contract for every designer (designer-doc@1): one document model with families per asset type (toolbar, banner, nav, app menu, context menu, flat) and asset round trips, ops, multi-select, map canvas (snap, align, distribute, auto layout, zoom), drag-and-drop (parseDrop / canDrop / applyDrop), undo / redo with coalescing, the designer context menu + keyboard map

asset-context@1: the context-menu section every UI asset gets (identity with tooltip, live Preview entry, About, Help, Edit in its designer, Copy id, Where used) and assetInfo in every mode (tooltip, hover card, side panel, help text, say); MenuEntry gains tip / preview / disabled; data-axf-asset attribute contract

Fixtures + validators + checks: spec/fixtures/designer.json replayed by spec/check-designer.mjs (CI), both validators agree, starters (designer ×7, settings ×7, embed ×3), JSON Schemas, re-bake + shared-assets bake, PORTING.md row, DESIGNER.md spec, report, Opus steps written into the plan

origin.said:
# Icon Browser + Icon Manager (Brett, voice)

## 1. Icon Browser plugin
- Ship a starter library: download a couple thousand icons (open-licensed sets), stored as assets.
- Views: tree, grid, list, etc. Categorized, sortable, filterable, searchable. Tree thumbnails toggle on/off.
- Sources (configurable, any type): FTP/SFTP (credentials + root folder), MCP, REST API, HTTP/online, local folder, Google Drive folder, Google Photos album, Dropbox, etc. Per-type config form: credentials when needed, root/path, auth. 'Online' shows a big list of known icon repositories, each with a section for what's needed to access it (API key etc.). Secrets in the secure store.
- Packs: create icon packs by drag and drop between panes. Panes are collapsible and floatable.
- Tab groups: open one or many selected icons into a floating tab group, a docked tab group, or a pane. 'Open new tab group' spawns docked or floating; with a selection it holds those icons, empty it shows a + to add. Drag icons from tree to groups and group to group.
- Save a pack as an icon-pack asset.

## 2. Icon Manager
- Every UI and plugin gets an icon map (icon slots/tags -> icon). All of AmberX, Console, axHub, everything.
- List/grid of every UI with an icon map, filterable by app. Open a map, or open a live preview of the UI and drag icons onto the preview. Save / Apply makes it permanent for that icon tag.
- Global icon pack asset listing every icon in the whole system.
- Inheritance: assign a pack to the whole app (root), or per UI, or per plugin. The child overrides the parent.
- Save changes as a new pack: root/global pack, or a UI/plugin-scoped pack.
- Icon packs are separate from design/style packs. A design pack MAY reference an icon pack but does not have to.
- Switch packs globally; a randomize button reshuffles the whole icon set; generate cohesive packs that follow one theme/style.

## Rules
- Everything is registry assets, with API/MCP/CLI parity and voice control.
- Settings in categorized collapsible sections.
- Submit UI options to UI Review first (at least 3).

steps.text: Contracts: icon-map@1 (slots -> icon refs, scope app | ui | plugin, extends, inheritance child over parent) and icon-source@1 (kind, config, secretRef) asset types in asset-types.json; iconmap-rules.mjs + .d.mts (normalize, errors, ref parsing name | pack:<id>/<glyph>, resolve chain, randomize, cohesive generation), engine iconmap.ts exported from core; fixture spec/fixtures/icon-map.json + check-icon-map.mts; starter assets; validate --framework and schemas green; Kotlin twin recorded as deferred in PORTING.md

Icon library: framework/cli/icon-import.mjs (SVG -> icon-pack glyphs: path, circle, ellipse, rect, line, polyline, polygon; 24 grid; <= 600 glyphs per pack, sets split by category) downloads open-licensed sets (Lucide ISC, Tabler MIT, Feather MIT, Heroicons MIT, Bootstrap Icons MIT, Phosphor MIT) from npm into framework/icon-library/ (icon-library@1 index.json: sets -> packs, licence, counts, categories, tags), every pack a valid icon-pack@1; `icon-import.mjs library --check` (valid, in sync, size budget) wired into CI

Runtime: rt.iconFor(name, scope) resolves through the icon maps (plugin / UI map -> app root map -> active icon pack -> framework glyph), React IconScope context, Icon.tsx reads it; settings keys axf.icons.* (map picks per scope, slot overrides) count as appearance settings so the hub look carries them to every app; actions icons.set | icons.apply | icons.pack | icons.randomize | icons.generate | icons.reset registered for voice / MCP / CLI; check-icon-map covers the runtime path

Icon Browser plugin core (apps/console-web/plugins/icon-browser): plugin.json (lifecycle, commands block, help.json, builtWith), server part (library index + search from framework/icon-library, sources CRUD, private secret store in the data dir, packs save as icon-pack assets, maps list), web: page head, tree / grid / list views with categories, sort, filter, search, thumbnails toggle, virtualised grid; menu.ts entries; settings tab in categorized collapsible sections

Panes, packs and tab groups: collapsible / floatable panes (library, pack composer, details) on the dock engine; drag icons between panes to compose a pack; Save pack as an icon-pack asset (server writes it, runtime registers it); open one or many selected icons into a docked or floating tab group or a pane through WindowManager (openGroup / openFloating / addTab); 'Open new tab group' docked or floating, empty shows a + to add; drag tree -> group and group -> group

Icon Manager page: list / grid of every UI with an icon map (console, plugins, axHub web, AmberX, Molly), filterable by app; map editor (slot -> icon, drops from the browser); live preview of the UI with drops onto its icons; Save / Apply makes the pick permanent for that slot; inheritance view (root -> UI -> plugin, child overrides); assign a pack at root, UI or plugin; Save changes as a new root / scoped pack; global 'every icon' pack; switch packs globally; Randomize; Generate cohesive pack (one set / style)

Sources: per-type config forms (local folder, HTTP, REST, MCP, FTP / SFTP, Google Drive, Google Photos, Dropbox, online repository) with credentials, root / path and auth; secrets saved to the plugin's private store by reference only; framework/schemas/icon-repos.json: the known online icon repositories with what each needs (API key, token, none) shown per repository; test connection; import from a source into the library

Icon maps for every app: framework/cli/icon-map.mjs scan | list | check scans the icon names each UI and plugin uses (console, plugins, axHub web, AmberX, Molly) and writes / updates their icon-map assets; CI check that no UI is without a map; MCP / CLI parity of the plugin commands checked (plugin-commands.mjs check)
Polish: help.json for every control, menu-reach, help-coverage, check-theme / check-controls / check-chrome-assets / plugin-lifecycle / plugin-pages green; settings sections finished; console re-bake
Screenshots (desktop + phone) of at least 3 UI options for the browser and the manager submitted to UI Review; report _claude/builds/reports/icon-browser-manager.md; THREADS.md; PR opened and linked

origin.said:
# Icon Browser + Icon Manager (Brett, voice)

## 1. Icon Browser plugin
- Ship a starter library: download a couple thousand icons (open-licensed sets), stored as assets.
- Views: tree, grid, list, etc. Categorized, sortable, filterable, searchable. Tree thumbnails toggle on/off.
- Sources (configurable, any type): FTP/SFTP (credentials + root folder), MCP, REST API, HTTP/online, local folder, Google Drive folder, Google Photos album, Dropbox, etc. Per-type config form: credentials when needed, root/path, auth. 'Online' shows a big list of known icon repositories, each with a section for what's needed to access it (API key etc.). Secrets in the secure store.
- Packs: create icon packs by drag and drop between panes. Panes are collapsible and floatable.
- Tab groups: open one or many selected icons into a floating tab group, a docked tab group, or a pane. 'Open new tab group' spawns docked or floating; with a selection it holds those icons, empty it shows a + to add. Drag icons from tree to groups and group to group.
- Save a pack as an icon-pack asset.

## 2. Icon Manager
- Every UI and plugin gets an icon map (icon slots/tags -> icon). All of AmberX, Console, axHub, everything.
- List/grid of every UI with an icon map, filterable by app. Open a map, or open a live preview of the UI and drag icons onto the preview. Save / Apply makes it permanent for that icon tag.
- Global icon pack asset listing every icon in the whole system.
- Inheritance: assign a pack to the whole app (root), or per UI, or per plugin. The child overrides the parent.
- Save changes as a new pack: root/global pack, or a UI/plugin-scoped pack.
- Icon packs are separate from design/style packs. A design pack MAY reference an icon pack but does not have to.
- Switch packs globally; a randomize button reshuffles the whole icon set; generate cohesive packs that follow one theme/style.

## Rules
- Everything is registry assets, with API/MCP/CLI parity and voice control.
- Settings in categorized collapsible sections.
- Submit UI options to UI Review first (at least 3).

steps.text: Contracts: icon-map@1 (slots -> icon refs, scope app | ui | plugin, extends, inheritance child over parent) and icon-source@1 (kind, config, secretRef) asset types in asset-types.json; iconmap-rules.mjs + .d.mts (normalize, errors, ref parsing name | pack:<id>/<glyph>, resolve chain, randomize, cohesive generation), engine iconmap.ts exported from core; fixture spec/fixtures/icon-map.json + check-icon-map.mts; starter assets; validate --framework and schemas green; Kotlin twin recorded as deferred in PORTING.md

Icon library: framework/cli/icon-import.mjs (SVG -> icon-pack glyphs: path, circle, ellipse, rect, line, polyline, polygon; 24 grid; <= 600 glyphs per pack, sets split by category) downloads open-licensed sets (Lucide ISC, Tabler MIT, Feather MIT, Heroicons MIT, Bootstrap Icons MIT, Phosphor MIT) from npm into framework/icon-library/ (icon-library@1 index.json: sets -> packs, licence, counts, categories, tags), every pack a valid icon-pack@1; `icon-import.mjs library --check` (valid, in sync, size budget) wired into CI

Runtime: rt.iconFor(name, scope) resolves through the icon maps (plugin / UI map -> app root map -> active icon pack -> framework glyph), React IconScope context, Icon.tsx reads it; settings keys axf.icons.* (map picks per scope, slot overrides) count as appearance settings so the hub look carries them to every app; actions icons.set | icons.apply | icons.pack | icons.randomize | icons.generate | icons.reset registered for voice / MCP / CLI; check-icon-map covers the runtime path

Icon Browser plugin core (apps/console-web/plugins/icon-browser): plugin.json (lifecycle, commands block, help.json, builtWith), server part (library index + search from framework/icon-library, sources CRUD, private secret store in the data dir, packs save as icon-pack assets, maps list), web: page head, tree / grid / list views with categories, sort, filter, search, thumbnails toggle, virtualised grid; menu.ts entries; settings tab in categorized collapsible sections

Panes, packs and tab groups: collapsible / floatable panes (library, pack composer, details) on the dock engine; drag icons between panes to compose a pack; Save pack as an icon-pack asset (server writes it, runtime registers it); open one or many selected icons into a docked or floating tab group or a pane through WindowManager (openGroup / openFloating / addTab); 'Open new tab group' docked or floating, empty shows a + to add; drag tree -> group and group -> group

Icon Manager page: list / grid of every UI with an icon map (console, plugins, axHub web, AmberX, Molly), filterable by app; map editor (slot -> icon, drops from the browser); live preview of the UI with drops onto its icons; Save / Apply makes the pick permanent for that slot; inheritance view (root -> UI -> plugin, child overrides); assign a pack at root, UI or plugin; Save changes as a new root / scoped pack; global 'every icon' pack; switch packs globally; Randomize; Generate cohesive pack (one set / style)

Sources: per-type config forms (local folder, HTTP, REST, MCP, FTP / SFTP, Google Drive, Google Photos, Dropbox, online repository) with credentials, root / path and auth; secrets saved to the plugin's private store by reference only; framework/schemas/icon-repos.json: the known online icon repositories with what each needs (API key, token, none) shown per repository; test connection; import from a source into the library

Icon maps for every app: framework/cli/icon-map.mjs scan | list | check scans the icon names each UI and plugin uses (console, plugins, axHub web, AmberX, Molly) and writes / updates their icon-map assets; CI check that no UI is without a map; MCP / CLI parity of the plugin commands checked (plugin-commands.mjs check)
Polish: help.json for every control, menu-reach, help-coverage, check-theme / check-controls / check-chrome-assets / plugin-lifecycle / plugin-pages green; settings sections finished; console re-bake
Screenshots (desktop + phone) of at least 3 UI options for the browser and the manager submitted to UI Review; report _claude/builds/reports/icon-browser-manager.md; THREADS.md; PR opened and linked

Opus phase: the host plugin, six standalone add-on plugins, voice + API/MCP/CLI, tests, UI Review. Plan Studio: Proposed > Assets (proposed-fzf3). Supersedes the menu / toolbar editors of the old asset-designer pending build.

origin.said: "We're gonna build a UI asset designer, which will create assets with their manifest and their identifier. It's going to create separate plugins for the app menu designer, the nav menu designer, the toolbar designer, the banner designer, the embedded widget designer, the widget designer. These are not dependent on the designer, but the designer interface will inherit those other designers. The UI designer plugin will have add-ons, each with their own settings interface and the designer's interface." "Redo them all from scratch." "Make it a build and get the Fable stuff going. Make it super powerful: full-blown context menu, drag and drop, map-based. Every UI asset will also have a context menu section which gives you a preview of the UI, and informs you in multiple ways (tooltips etc)."

steps.text: designer@1 contract: host + add-on model (designer-addon@1: id, asset types, designer UI view, settings interface asset, designer interface asset, manifest fields, capabilities, drops, voice), the designer asset type (the designer's interface with inherit@1 copies per add-on), rules file + .d.mts, exported from core

Asset output contract: designed@1 manifest + stable identifier (uid, ref, revision, hash, origin), registration as a ui-registry@1 item (coordinated with ui-registry-shortcuts, no duplicate engine) and in the designer library index (designer-library@1, paths per output target); the embed asset type (embed-asset@1)

Interaction contract for every designer (designer-doc@1): one document model with families per asset type (toolbar, banner, nav, app menu, context menu, flat) and asset round trips, ops, multi-select, map canvas (snap, align, distribute, auto layout, zoom), drag-and-drop (parseDrop / canDrop / applyDrop), undo / redo with coalescing, the designer context menu + keyboard map

asset-context@1: the context-menu section every UI asset gets (identity with tooltip, live Preview entry, About, Help, Edit in its designer, Copy id, Where used) and assetInfo in every mode (tooltip, hover card, side panel, help text, say); MenuEntry gains tip / preview / disabled; data-axf-asset attribute contract

Fixtures + validators + checks: spec/fixtures/designer.json replayed by spec/check-designer.mjs (CI), both validators agree, starters (designer ×7, settings ×7, embed ×3), JSON Schemas, re-bake + shared-assets bake, PORTING.md row, DESIGNER.md spec, report, Opus steps written into the plan
PR into the merge queue (never landed directly), THREADS.md + STATUS.md + decisions.md, build linked (builds-live.mjs link)

Host plugin skeleton: plugins/ui-asset-designer from _template (id ai.amberx.axf.console.ui-asset-designer, uiEditor builder, lifecycle, install/uninstall, provides service:axf.designer@1), nav Plugins → UI asset designer, Settings → Plugins sub-tab rendered through settings/designer; plugin-lifecycle check passes

Host server (FastAPI): capability axf.designer@1 (addons, library, get, validate, save, register, preview), designer-library@1 index in the lifecycle dataDir, saves through makeDesigned / withDesigned, built-in ids refused, plugin-commands@1 auto routes; test.py

Host web shell: add-on list (designerAddonChoices, installed / missing with a link to the plugin), asset library panel (designed + built-in per type, search, New / Open / Duplicate / Delete), designer interface + settings interface pickers (inherit@1 copies, Reset to default)

Shared designer shell: map canvas (free / flow / both, grid, snap, rulers, guides, zoom) + layers tree on designerDoc with multi-select (click / ctrl / shift / marquee), drag within the tree and the map, panels placed by the designer interface (left / right / bottom / float / hidden)

Shared inspector from nodeProps (text, icon picker, action picker from rt.actions, view picker from the UI registry, bindings, choices, numbers) + root data fields from asset-types.json; the chrome settings dialog pattern for the designer interface (Settings…)

Shared context menu + keyboard: designerContextMenu entries (tip tooltips, disabled, submenus) on right-click / long-press of nodes and the canvas, DESIGNER_KEYS handling, clipboard (cut / copy / paste within and across designers), undo / redo on createHistory / commit with coalescing from the interface

Shared drag-and-drop in and out: parseDrop / canDrop / applyDrop for palette items, assets from the library, actions, grid hooks (grid-hook@1), embeds, text, URLs and files; drop indicators (before / after / inside, map position); nodeDragPayload for dragging nodes out to other designers

Shared live preview: docked / floating / inline per the interface, desktop + phone frames, live or on-save refresh, through rt.swap on a preview id per type (never the app's real slot); AssetPreview miniature for the asset library cards

Save / publish flow: id suggestion + designedIdErrors, makeDesigned (origin = what Brett said when voice-started), version bump per the interface, library upsert, ui-registry.json declaration of the host (designedRegistryItem) + `ui-registry.mjs generate`, output target app / framework / hub, autosave

asset-context@1 in the runtime: contextExtras '*:asset' from data-axf-asset on every chrome, widget, dialog and embed element (Chrome.tsx, Widgets.tsx, TabGroup.tsx, Overlays.tsx carry the attribute), assetContextSection with the add-on in force, actions asset.preview / asset.about / asset.copyId / asset.usage registered, help@1 entries from assetInfo help-text

Menu rendering of the new entry fields: MenuList / Overlays draw tip (tooltip + Help mode), preview (a live miniature of the asset on hover: AssetPreview in a popover), disabled; About opens the hover card (phone: sheet) and the side panel; Where used lists hosts from the live chrome

after.title: Icon Browser plugin + Icon Manager (icon library, icon maps, icon packs)
after.detail: Icon Browser plugin: starter library of open-licensed icon sets stored as icon-pack assets (framework/icon-library, served by the plugin, never bundled); tree / grid / list views with categories, sort, filter, search and a thumbnails toggle; configurable sources of any kind (local, HTTP, REST, MCP, FTP/SFTP, Google Drive, Google Photos, Dropbox, known online repositories) with per-type forms and secrets in the plugin's private store; packs composed by drag and drop between collapsible / floatable panes; selected icons open into docked or floating tab groups; packs saved as icon-pack assets. Icon Manager: every UI and plugin has an icon map (icon-map@1: slot -> icon ref, inheritance app root -> UI -> plugin, child overrides parent); list / grid of every UI with a map, filterable by app; map editor + live preview with drops; Save / Apply; a global pack listing every icon; switch packs globally, randomize, generate cohesive packs. Everything is assets with API / MCP / CLI parity and voice actions; settings in categorized collapsible sections; UI options to UI Review first (3+).

notes.text: Launched headless on Fable by Brett from the Build manager (agent Gina, change chg-20261107-a5722a8eb3). Phase 1 (s1-s6) runs on Fable; s7-s10 are Opus: at that switch the session stops and hands over the brief (downgrade, no approval).

origin.said:
# Icon Browser + Icon Manager (Brett, voice)

## 1. Icon Browser plugin
- Ship a starter library: download a couple thousand icons (open-licensed sets), stored as assets.
- Views: tree, grid, list, etc. Categorized, sortable, filterable, searchable. Tree thumbnails toggle on/off.
- Sources (configurable, any type): FTP/SFTP (credentials + root folder), MCP, REST API, HTTP/online, local folder, Google Drive folder, Google Photos album, Dropbox, etc. Per-type config form: credentials when needed, root/path, auth. 'Online' shows a big list of known icon repositories, each with a section for what's needed to access it (API key etc.). Secrets in the secure store.
- Packs: create icon packs by drag and drop between panes. Panes are collapsible and floatable.
- Tab groups: open one or many selected icons into a floating tab group, a docked tab group, or a pane. 'Open new tab group' spawns docked or floating; with a selection it holds those icons, empty it shows a + to add. Drag icons from tree to groups and group to group.
- Save a pack as an icon-pack asset.

## 2. Icon Manager
- Every UI and plugin gets an icon map (icon slots/tags -> icon). All of AmberX, Console, axHub, everything.
- List/grid of every UI with an icon map, filterable by app. Open a map, or open a live preview of the UI and drag icons onto the preview. Save / Apply makes it permanent for that icon tag.
- Global icon pack asset listing every icon in the whole system.
- Inheritance: assign a pack to the whole app (root), or per UI, or per plugin. The child overrides the parent.
- Save changes as a new pack: root/global pack, or a UI/plugin-scoped pack.
- Icon packs are separate from design/style packs. A design pack MAY reference an icon pack but does not have to.
- Switch packs globally; a randomize button reshuffles the whole icon set; generate cohesive packs that follow one theme/style.

## Rules
- Everything is registry assets, with API/MCP/CLI parity and voice control.
- Settings in categorized collapsible sections.
- Submit UI options to UI Review first (at least 3).

steps.text: Contracts: icon-map@1 (slots -> icon refs, scope app | ui | plugin, extends, inheritance child over parent) and icon-source@1 (kind, config, secretRef) asset types in asset-types.json; iconmap-rules.mjs + .d.mts (normalize, errors, ref parsing name | pack:<id>/<glyph>, resolve chain, randomize, cohesive generation), engine iconmap.ts exported from core; fixture spec/fixtures/icon-map.json + check-icon-map.mts; starter assets; validate --framework and schemas green; Kotlin twin recorded as deferred in PORTING.md

Icon library: framework/cli/icon-import.mjs (SVG -> icon-pack glyphs: path, circle, ellipse, rect, line, polyline, polygon; 24 grid; <= 600 glyphs per pack, sets split by category) downloads open-licensed sets (Lucide ISC, Tabler MIT, Feather MIT, Heroicons MIT, Bootstrap Icons MIT, Phosphor MIT) from npm into framework/icon-library/ (icon-library@1 index.json: sets -> packs, licence, counts, categories, tags), every pack a valid icon-pack@1; `icon-import.mjs library --check` (valid, in sync, size budget) wired into CI

Runtime: rt.iconFor(name, scope) resolves through the icon maps (plugin / UI map -> app root map -> active icon pack -> framework glyph), React IconScope context, Icon.tsx reads it; settings keys axf.icons.* (map picks per scope, slot overrides) count as appearance settings so the hub look carries them to every app; actions icons.set | icons.apply | icons.pack | icons.randomize | icons.generate | icons.reset registered for voice / MCP / CLI; check-icon-map covers the runtime path

Icon Browser plugin core (apps/console-web/plugins/icon-browser): plugin.json (lifecycle, commands block, help.json, builtWith), server part (library index + search from framework/icon-library, sources CRUD, private secret store in the data dir, packs save as icon-pack assets, maps list), web: page head, tree / grid / list views with categories, sort, filter, search, thumbnails toggle, virtualised grid; menu.ts entries; settings tab in categorized collapsible sections

Panes, packs and tab groups: collapsible / floatable panes (library, pack composer, details) on the dock engine; drag icons between panes to compose a pack; Save pack as an icon-pack asset (server writes it, runtime registers it); open one or many selected icons into a docked or floating tab group or a pane through WindowManager (openGroup / openFloating / addTab); 'Open new tab group' docked or floating, empty shows a + to add; drag tree -> group and group -> group

before.detail: Fable phase: designer@1 contracts (add-on model, designer + embed asset types, designed@1 manifest + identifier + registration, designer-doc@1 interaction contract, asset-context@1 section), fixtures, validators, checks, PORTING.md, DESIGNER.md. origin.said: "We're gonna build a UI asset designer, which will create assets with their manifest and their identifier. It's going to create separate plugins for the app menu designer, the nav menu designer, the toolbar designer, the banner designer, the embedded widget designer, the widget designer. These are not dependent on the designer, but the designer interface will inherit those other designers. The UI designer plugin will have add-ons, each with their own settings interface and the designer's interface." "Redo them all from scratch." "Make it a build and get the Fable stuff going. Make it super powerful: full-blown context menu, drag and drop, map-based. Every UI asset will also have a context menu section which gives you a preview of the UI, and informs you in multiple ways (tooltips etc)."

steps.text: designer@1 contract: host + add-on model (designer-addon@1: id, asset types, designer UI view, settings interface asset, designer interface asset, manifest fields, capabilities, drops, voice), the designer asset type (the designer's interface with inherit@1 copies per add-on), rules file + .d.mts, exported from core

Asset output contract: designed@1 manifest + stable identifier (uid, ref, revision, hash, origin), registration as a ui-registry@1 item (coordinated with ui-registry-shortcuts, no duplicate engine) and in the designer library index (designer-library@1, paths per output target); the embed asset type (embed-asset@1)

Interaction contract for every designer (designer-doc@1): one document model with families per asset type (toolbar, banner, nav, app menu, context menu, flat) and asset round trips, ops, multi-select, map canvas (snap, align, distribute, auto layout, zoom), drag-and-drop (parseDrop / canDrop / applyDrop), undo / redo with coalescing, the designer context menu + keyboard map

asset-context@1: the context-menu section every UI asset gets (identity with tooltip, live Preview entry, About, Help, Edit in its designer, Copy id, Where used) and assetInfo in every mode (tooltip, hover card, side panel, help text, say); MenuEntry gains tip / preview / disabled; data-axf-asset attribute contract

Fixtures + validators + checks: spec/fixtures/designer.json replayed by spec/check-designer.mjs (CI), both validators agree, starters (designer ×7, settings ×7, embed ×3), JSON Schemas, re-bake + shared-assets bake, PORTING.md row, DESIGNER.md spec, report, Opus steps written into the plan
PR into the merge queue (never landed directly), THREADS.md + STATUS.md + decisions.md, build linked (builds-live.mjs link)

Host web shell: add-on list (designerAddonChoices, installed / missing with a link to the plugin), asset library panel (designed + built-in per type, search, New / Open / Duplicate / Delete), designer interface + settings interface pickers (inherit@1 copies, Reset to default)

Shared designer shell: map canvas (free / flow / both, grid, snap, rulers, guides, zoom) + layers tree on designerDoc with multi-select (click / ctrl / shift / marquee), drag within the tree and the map, panels placed by the designer interface (left / right / bottom / float / hidden)

Shared inspector from nodeProps (text, icon picker, action picker from rt.actions, view picker from the UI registry, bindings, choices, numbers) + root data fields from asset-types.json; the chrome settings dialog pattern for the designer interface (Settings…)

Shared context menu + keyboard: designerContextMenu entries (tip tooltips, disabled, submenus) on right-click / long-press of nodes and the canvas, DESIGNER_KEYS handling, clipboard (cut / copy / paste within and across designers), undo / redo on createHistory / commit with coalescing from the interface

Shared drag-and-drop in and out: parseDrop / canDrop / applyDrop for palette items, assets from the library, actions, grid hooks (grid-hook@1), embeds, text, URLs and files; drop indicators (before / after / inside, map position); nodeDragPayload for dragging nodes out to other designers

Shared live preview: docked / floating / inline per the interface, desktop + phone frames, live or on-save refresh, through rt.swap on a preview id per type (never the app's real slot); AssetPreview miniature for the asset library cards

It's going to create separate plugins for the app menu designer, the nav menu designer, the toolbar designer, the banner designer, the embedded widget designer, the widget designer. These are not dependent on the designer, but the designer interface will inherit those other designers. The UI designer plugin will have add-ons, each with their own settings interface and the designer's interface." "Redo them all from scratch." "Make it a build and get the Fable stuff going. Make it super powerful: full-blown context menu, drag and drop, map-based. Every UI asset will also have a context menu section which gives you a preview of the UI, and informs you in multiple ways (tooltips etc)."

steps.text: designer@1 contract: host + add-on model (designer-addon@1: id, asset types, designer UI view, settings interface asset, designer interface asset, manifest fields, capabilities, drops, voice), the designer asset type (the designer's interface with inherit@1 copies per add-on), rules file + .d.mts, exported from core

Asset output contract: designed@1 manifest + stable identifier (uid, ref, revision, hash, origin), registration as a ui-registry@1 item (coordinated with ui-registry-shortcuts, no duplicate engine) and in the designer library index (designer-library@1, paths per output target); the embed asset type (embed-asset@1)

Interaction contract for every designer (designer-doc@1): one document model with families per asset type (toolbar, banner, nav, app menu, context menu, flat) and asset round trips, ops, multi-select, map canvas (snap, align, distribute, auto layout, zoom), drag-and-drop (parseDrop / canDrop / applyDrop), undo / redo with coalescing, the designer context menu + keyboard map

asset-context@1: the context-menu section every UI asset gets (identity with tooltip, live Preview entry, About, Help, Edit in its designer, Copy id, Where used) and assetInfo in every mode (tooltip, hover card, side panel, help text, say); MenuEntry gains tip / preview / disabled; data-axf-asset attribute contract

Fixtures + validators + checks: spec/fixtures/designer.json replayed by spec/check-designer.mjs (CI), both validators agree, starters (designer ×7, settings ×7, embed ×3), JSON Schemas, re-bake + shared-assets bake, PORTING.md row, DESIGNER.md spec, report, Opus steps written into the plan
PR into the merge queue (never landed directly), THREADS.md + STATUS.md + decisions.md, build linked (builds-live.mjs link)

Host server (FastAPI): capability axf.designer@1 (addons, library, get, validate, save, register, preview), designer-library@1 index in the lifecycle dataDir, saves through makeDesigned / withDesigned, built-in ids refused, plugin-commands@1 auto routes; test.py

Host web shell: add-on list (designerAddonChoices, installed / missing with a link to the plugin), asset library panel (designed + built-in per type, search, New / Open / Duplicate / Delete), designer interface + settings interface pickers (inherit@1 copies, Reset to default)

Shared designer shell: map canvas (free / flow / both, grid, snap, rulers, guides, zoom) + layers tree on designerDoc with multi-select (click / ctrl / shift / marquee), drag within the tree and the map, panels placed by the designer interface (left / right / bottom / float / hidden)

Shared inspector from nodeProps (text, icon picker, action picker from rt.actions, view picker from the UI registry, bindings, choices, numbers) + root data fields from asset-types.json; the chrome settings dialog pattern for the designer interface (Settings…)

Shared context menu + keyboard: designerContextMenu entries (tip tooltips, disabled, submenus) on right-click / long-press of nodes and the canvas, DESIGNER_KEYS handling, clipboard (cut / copy / paste within and across designers), undo / redo on createHistory / commit with coalescing from the interface

Shared drag-and-drop in and out: parseDrop / canDrop / applyDrop for palette items, assets from the library, actions, grid hooks (grid-hook@1), embeds, text, URLs and files; drop indicators (before / after / inside, map position); nodeDragPayload for dragging nodes out to other designers

Shared live preview: docked / floating / inline per the interface, desktop + phone frames, live or on-save refresh, through rt.swap on a preview id per type (never the app's real slot); AssetPreview miniature for the asset library cards

Save / publish flow: id suggestion + designedIdErrors, makeDesigned (origin = what Brett said when voice-started), version bump per the interface, library upsert, ui-registry.json declaration of the host (designedRegistryItem) + `ui-registry.mjs generate`, output target app / framework / hub, autosave

asset-context@1 in the runtime: contextExtras '*:asset' from data-axf-asset on every chrome, widget, dialog and embed element (Chrome.tsx, Widgets.tsx, TabGroup.tsx, Overlays.tsx carry the attribute), assetContextSection with the add-on in force, actions asset.preview / asset.about / asset.copyId / asset.usage registered, help@1 entries from assetInfo help-text

origin.said:
# Icon Browser + Icon Manager (Brett, voice)

## 1. Icon Browser plugin
- Ship a starter library: download a couple thousand icons (open-licensed sets), stored as assets.
- Views: tree, grid, list, etc. Categorized, sortable, filterable, searchable. Tree thumbnails toggle on/off.
- Sources (configurable, any type): FTP/SFTP (credentials + root folder), MCP, REST API, HTTP/online, local folder, Google Drive folder, Google Photos album, Dropbox, etc. Per-type config form: credentials when needed, root/path, auth. 'Online' shows a big list of known icon repositories, each with a section for what's needed to access it (API key etc.). Secrets in the secure store.
- Packs: create icon packs by drag and drop between panes. Panes are collapsible and floatable.
- Tab groups: open one or many selected icons into a floating tab group, a docked tab group, or a pane. 'Open new tab group' spawns docked or floating; with a selection it holds those icons, empty it shows a + to add. Drag icons from tree to groups and group to group.
- Save a pack as an icon-pack asset.

## 2. Icon Manager
- Every UI and plugin gets an icon map (icon slots/tags -> icon). All of AmberX, Console, axHub, everything.
- List/grid of every UI with an icon map, filterable by app. Open a map, or open a live preview of the UI and drag icons onto the preview. Save / Apply makes it permanent for that icon tag.
- Global icon pack asset listing every icon in the whole system.
- Inheritance: assign a pack to the whole app (root), or per UI, or per plugin. The child overrides the parent.
- Save changes as a new pack: root/global pack, or a UI/plugin-scoped pack.
- Icon packs are separate from design/style packs. A design pack MAY reference an icon pack but does not have to.
- Switch packs globally; a randomize button reshuffles the whole icon set; generate cohesive packs that follow one theme/style.

## Rules
- Everything is registry assets, with API/MCP/CLI parity and voice control.
- Settings in categorized collapsible sections.
- Submit UI options to UI Review first (at least 3).

steps.text: Contracts: icon-map@1 (slots -> icon refs, scope app | ui | plugin, extends, inheritance child over parent) and icon-source@1 (kind, config, secretRef) asset types in asset-types.json; iconmap-rules.mjs + .d.mts (normalize, errors, ref parsing name | pack:<id>/<glyph>, resolve chain, randomize, cohesive generation), engine iconmap.ts exported from core; fixture spec/fixtures/icon-map.json + check-icon-map.mts; starter assets; validate --framework and schemas green; Kotlin twin recorded as deferred in PORTING.md

Icon library: framework/cli/icon-import.mjs (SVG -> icon-pack glyphs: path, circle, ellipse, rect, line, polyline, polygon; 24 grid; <= 600 glyphs per pack, sets split by category) downloads open-licensed sets (Lucide ISC, Tabler MIT, Feather MIT, Heroicons MIT, Bootstrap Icons MIT, Phosphor MIT) from npm into framework/icon-library/ (icon-library@1 index.json: sets -> packs, licence, counts, categories, tags), every pack a valid icon-pack@1; `icon-import.mjs library --check` (valid, in sync, size budget) wired into CI

Runtime: rt.iconFor(name, scope) resolves through the icon maps (plugin / UI map -> app root map -> active icon pack -> framework glyph), React IconScope context, Icon.tsx reads it; settings keys axf.icons.* (map picks per scope, slot overrides) count as appearance settings so the hub look carries them to every app; actions icons.set | icons.apply | icons.pack | icons.randomize | icons.generate | icons.reset registered for voice / MCP / CLI; check-icon-map covers the runtime path

Icon Browser plugin core (apps/console-web/plugins/icon-browser): plugin.json (lifecycle, commands block, help.json, builtWith), server part (library index + search from framework/icon-library, sources CRUD, private secret store in the data dir, packs save as icon-pack assets, maps list), web: page head, tree / grid / list views with categories, sort, filter, search, thumbnails toggle, virtualised grid; menu.ts entries; settings tab in categorized collapsible sections

Panes, packs and tab groups: collapsible / floatable panes (library, pack composer, details) on the dock engine; drag icons between panes to compose a pack; Save pack as an icon-pack asset (server writes it, runtime registers it); open one or many selected icons into a docked or floating tab group or a pane through WindowManager (openGroup / openFloating / addTab); 'Open new tab group' docked or floating, empty shows a + to add; drag tree -> group and group -> group

Icon Manager page: list / grid of every UI with an icon map (console, plugins, axHub web, AmberX, Molly), filterable by app; map editor (slot -> icon, drops from the browser); live preview of the UI with drops onto its icons; Save / Apply makes the pick permanent for that slot; inheritance view (root -> UI -> plugin, child overrides); assign a pack at root, UI or plugin; Save changes as a new root / scoped pack; global 'every icon' pack; switch packs globally; Randomize; Generate cohesive pack (one set / style)

Sources: per-type config forms (local folder, HTTP, REST, MCP, FTP / SFTP, Google Drive, Google Photos, Dropbox, online repository) with credentials, root / path and auth; secrets saved to the plugin's private store by reference only; framework/schemas/icon-repos.json: the known online icon repositories with what each needs (API key, token, none) shown per repository; test connection; import from a source into the library

Icon maps for every app: framework/cli/icon-map.mjs scan | list | check scans the icon names each UI and plugin uses (console, plugins, axHub web, AmberX, Molly) and writes / updates their icon-map assets; CI check that no UI is without a map; MCP / CLI parity of the plugin commands checked (plugin-commands.mjs check)
Polish: help.json for every control, menu-reach, help-coverage, check-theme / check-controls / check-chrome-assets / plugin-lifecycle / plugin-pages green; settings sections finished; console re-bake
Screenshots (desktop + phone) of at least 3 UI options for the browser and the manager submitted to UI Review; report _claude/builds/reports/icon-browser-manager.md; THREADS.md; PR opened and linked

origin.said:
# Icon Browser + Icon Manager (Brett, voice)

## 1. Icon Browser plugin
- Ship a starter library: download a couple thousand icons (open-licensed sets), stored as assets.
- Views: tree, grid, list, etc. Categorized, sortable, filterable, searchable. Tree thumbnails toggle on/off.
- Sources (configurable, any type): FTP/SFTP (credentials + root folder), MCP, REST API, HTTP/online, local folder, Google Drive folder, Google Photos album, Dropbox, etc. Per-type config form: credentials when needed, root/path, auth. 'Online' shows a big list of known icon repositories, each with a section for what's needed to access it (API key etc.). Secrets in the secure store.
- Packs: create icon packs by drag and drop between panes. Panes are collapsible and floatable.
- Tab groups: open one or many selected icons into a floating tab group, a docked tab group, or a pane. 'Open new tab group' spawns docked or floating; with a selection it holds those icons, empty it shows a + to add. Drag icons from tree to groups and group to group.
- Save a pack as an icon-pack asset.

## 2. Icon Manager
- Every UI and plugin gets an icon map (icon slots/tags -> icon). All of AmberX, Console, axHub, everything.
- List/grid of every UI with an icon map, filterable by app. Open a map, or open a live preview of the UI and drag icons onto the preview. Save / Apply makes it permanent for that icon tag.
- Global icon pack asset listing every icon in the whole system.
- Inheritance: assign a pack to the whole app (root), or per UI, or per plugin. The child overrides the parent.
- Save changes as a new pack: root/global pack, or a UI/plugin-scoped pack.
- Icon packs are separate from design/style packs. A design pack MAY reference an icon pack but does not have to.
- Switch packs globally; a randomize button reshuffles the whole icon set; generate cohesive packs that follow one theme/style.

## Rules
- Everything is registry assets, with API/MCP/CLI parity and voice control.
- Settings in categorized collapsible sections.
- Submit UI options to UI Review first (at least 3).

steps.text: Contracts: icon-map@1 (slots -> icon refs, scope app | ui | plugin, extends, inheritance child over parent) and icon-source@1 (kind, config, secretRef) asset types in asset-types.json; iconmap-rules.mjs + .d.mts (normalize, errors, ref parsing name | pack:<id>/<glyph>, resolve chain, randomize, cohesive generation), engine iconmap.ts exported from core; fixture spec/fixtures/icon-map.json + check-icon-map.mts; starter assets; validate --framework and schemas green; Kotlin twin recorded as deferred in PORTING.md

Icon library: framework/cli/icon-import.mjs (SVG -> icon-pack glyphs: path, circle, ellipse, rect, line, polyline, polygon; 24 grid; <= 600 glyphs per pack, sets split by category) downloads open-licensed sets (Lucide ISC, Tabler MIT, Feather MIT, Heroicons MIT, Bootstrap Icons MIT, Phosphor MIT) from npm into framework/icon-library/ (icon-library@1 index.json: sets -> packs, licence, counts, categories, tags), every pack a valid icon-pack@1; `icon-import.mjs library --check` (valid, in sync, size budget) wired into CI

Runtime: rt.iconFor(name, scope) resolves through the icon maps (plugin / UI map -> app root map -> active icon pack -> framework glyph), React IconScope context, Icon.tsx reads it; settings keys axf.icons.* (map picks per scope, slot overrides) count as appearance settings so the hub look carries them to every app; actions icons.set | icons.apply | icons.pack | icons.randomize | icons.generate | icons.reset registered for voice / MCP / CLI; check-icon-map covers the runtime path

Icon Browser plugin core (apps/console-web/plugins/icon-browser): plugin.json (lifecycle, commands block, help.json, builtWith), server part (library index + search from framework/icon-library, sources CRUD, private secret store in the data dir, packs save as icon-pack assets, maps list), web: page head, tree / grid / list views with categories, sort, filter, search, thumbnails toggle, virtualised grid; menu.ts entries; settings tab in categorized collapsible sections

Panes, packs and tab groups: collapsible / floatable panes (library, pack composer, details) on the dock engine; drag icons between panes to compose a pack; Save pack as an icon-pack asset (server writes it, runtime registers it); open one or many selected icons into a docked or floating tab group or a pane through WindowManager (openGroup / openFloating / addTab); 'Open new tab group' docked or floating, empty shows a + to add; drag tree -> group and group -> group

Icon Manager page: list / grid of every UI with an icon map (console, plugins, axHub web, AmberX, Molly), filterable by app; map editor (slot -> icon, drops from the browser); live preview of the UI with drops onto its icons; Save / Apply makes the pick permanent for that slot; inheritance view (root -> UI -> plugin, child overrides); assign a pack at root, UI or plugin; Save changes as a new root / scoped pack; global 'every icon' pack; switch packs globally; Randomize; Generate cohesive pack (one set / style)

Sources: per-type config forms (local folder, HTTP, REST, MCP, FTP / SFTP, Google Drive, Google Photos, Dropbox, online repository) with credentials, root / path and auth; secrets saved to the plugin's private store by reference only; framework/schemas/icon-repos.json: the known online icon repositories with what each needs (API key, token, none) shown per repository; test connection; import from a source into the library

Icon maps for every app: framework/cli/icon-map.mjs scan | list | check scans the icon names each UI and plugin uses (console, plugins, axHub web, AmberX, Molly) and writes / updates their icon-map assets; CI check that no UI is without a map; MCP / CLI parity of the plugin commands checked (plugin-commands.mjs check)
Polish: help.json for every control, menu-reach, help-coverage, check-theme / check-controls / check-chrome-assets / plugin-lifecycle / plugin-pages green; settings sections finished; console re-bake
Screenshots (desktop + phone) of at least 3 UI options for the browser and the manager submitted to UI Review; report _claude/builds/reports/icon-browser-manager.md; THREADS.md; PR opened and linked
