origin.said: "We're gonna build a UI asset designer, which will create assets with their manifest and their identifier. It's going to create separate plugins for the app menu designer, the nav menu designer, the toolbar designer, the banner designer, the embedded widget designer, the widget designer. These are not dependent on the designer, but the designer interface will inherit those other designers. The UI designer plugin will have add-ons, each with their own settings interface and the designer's interface." "Redo them all from scratch." "Make it a build and get the Fable stuff going. Make it super powerful: full-blown context menu, drag and drop, map-based. Every UI asset will also have a context menu section which gives you a preview of the UI, and informs you in multiple ways (tooltips etc)."

steps.text: designer@1 contract: host + add-on model (designer-addon@1: id, asset types, designer UI view, settings interface asset, designer interface asset, manifest fields, capabilities, drops, voice), the designer asset type (the designer's interface with inherit@1 copies per add-on), rules file + .d.mts, exported from core

Asset output contract: designed@1 manifest + stable identifier (uid, ref, revision, hash, origin), registration as a ui-registry@1 item (coordinated with ui-registry-shortcuts, no duplicate engine) and in the designer library index (designer-library@1, paths per output target); the embed asset type (embed-asset@1)

Interaction contract for every designer (designer-doc@1): one document model with families per asset type (toolbar, banner, nav, app menu, context menu, flat) and asset round trips, ops, multi-select, map canvas (snap, align, distribute, auto layout, zoom), drag-and-drop (parseDrop / canDrop / applyDrop), undo / redo with coalescing, the designer context menu + keyboard map

asset-context@1: the context-menu section every UI asset gets (identity with tooltip, live Preview entry, About, Help, Edit in its designer, Copy id, Where used) and assetInfo in every mode (tooltip, hover card, side panel, help text, say); MenuEntry gains tip / preview / disabled; data-axf-asset attribute contract

Fixtures + validators + checks: spec/fixtures/designer.json replayed by spec/check-designer.mjs (CI), both validators agree, starters (designer ×7, settings ×7, embed ×3), JSON Schemas, re-bake + shared-assets bake, PORTING.md row, DESIGNER.md spec, report, Opus steps written into the plan
PR into the merge queue (never landed directly), THREADS.md + STATUS.md + decisions.md, build linked (builds-live.mjs link)

Host plugin skeleton: plugins/ui-asset-designer from _template (id ai.amberx.axf.console.ui-asset-designer, uiEditor builder, lifecycle, install/uninstall, provides service:axf.designer@1), nav Plugins → UI asset designer, Settings → Plugins sub-tab rendered through settings/designer; plugin-lifecycle check passes

Host server (FastAPI): capability axf.designer@1 (addons, library, get, validate, save, register, preview), designer-library@1 index in the lifecycle dataDir, saves through makeDesigned / withDesigned, built-in ids refused, plugin-commands@1 auto routes; test.py

Host web shell: add-on list (designerAddonChoices, installed / missing with a link to the plugin), asset library panel (designed + built-in per type, search, New / Open / Duplicate / Delete), designer interface + settings interface pickers (inherit@1 copies, Reset to default)

Shared designer shell: map canvas (free / flow / both, grid, snap, rulers, guides, zoom) + layers tree on designerDoc with multi-select (click / ctrl / shift / marquee), drag within the tree and the map, panels placed by the designer interface (left / right / bottom / float / hidden)

Shared inspector from nodeProps (text, icon picker, action picker from rt.actions, view picker from the UI registry, bindings, choices, numbers) + root data fields from asset-types.json; the chrome settings dialog pattern for the designer interface (Settings…)

Shared context menu + keyboard: designerContextMenu entries (tip tooltips, disabled, submenus) on right-click / long-press of nodes and the canvas, DESIGNER_KEYS handling, clipboard (cut / copy / paste within and across designers), undo / redo on createHistory / commit with coalescing from the interface

Shared drag-and-drop in and out: parseDrop / canDrop / applyDrop for palette items, assets from the library, actions, grid hooks (grid-hook@1), embeds, text, URLs and files; drop indicators (before / after / inside, map position); nodeDragPayload for dragging nodes out to other designers

Shared live preview: docked / floating / inline per the interface, desktop + phone frames, live or on-save refresh, through rt.swap on a preview id per type (never the app's real slot); AssetPreview miniature for the asset library cards

origin.brief:
# Build: claude-badge-vps

Brett (voice): "I need a setting in the Claude badge plugin that has a VPS connection and a console connection, and I need to be able to put them on icons only and select which icons for each one."

Claude badge plugin (apps/console-web/plugins/claude-badge):
1. Two connections, each its own badge/indicator on the banner:
   - Console connection: the existing test (console AI via axf.llm@1).
   - VPS connection: the Claude Code login on the VPS (which account, logged in or not, limit hit). Read it with plain code, zero tokens (e.g. the ai-keys/claude-accounts VPS status or a cheap read of /root/.claude.json email + credentials expiry); green = logged in and working, amber = limit hit / out of credits, gray/red = not logged in.
2. Settings (Settings > Plugins > Claude badge): show/hide each one; Icons only switch per badge; pick the icon for each badge and each state (ok / no credit / error), extending the existing Badge icons picker.
3. Covers step 18 of pending item token-usage-log-accounts-plan-studio-control (clock badge watches VPS login): note it there, don't build it twice.
4. Tests, README, screenshots to UI Review, PR to the merge queue. Do NOT land directly.

Nothing gets removed. One session for the whole build, read only files you need, no full CLAUDE.md chain. Stay out of notes/tasks/todo and AmberX notification code (other builds).
## UPDATE from Brett (replaces the scope above)
"I need the Claude badge, the axHub badge, the VPS badge and the AmberX badge, all in one plugin, all able to select which icon for which, and fully configurable."
- One plugin holds four badges: Claude (console AI), axHub (connection/health), VPS (Claude login on the VPS), AmberX (phone app connected/last seen). Move the existing ones in; old plugins can be disabled, nothing removed.
- Per badge: show/hide, icons only or icon + label, label text, icon per state (ok / warn / error / off), order on the banner.
- All plain-code checks, zero tokens.

## Addendum 2 (Brett, voice)
Add a usage meter for the Claude account signed in on the VPS (used out of total, 5-hour and weekly) to the same badge plugin, same options (show/hide, icon only, icons per state). Reuse the existing usage-meter widget code; don't build a second meter. This covers the 'Banner widget: usage meter of the account signed in on the VPS' step of token-usage-log-accounts-plan-studio-control-small-steps; note it there.

## Addendum 3 (Brett, voice)
"When we click that widget in the banner, it's gonna do whatever we have it set to do. Like, maybe it can drop down and show a list of all the accounts that are in console. It can show how many credits are left for all the accounts that are configured to connect to the VPS."
- Each badge/widget has a configurable tap action (setting): drop-down, open a screen, run a command, toggle, nothing.
- Usage meter default tap = drop-down listing every Claude account saved in the console/VPS: name, type, active marker, credits left (5-hour + weekly, reset time), status. Plain code reads, zero tokens; cached with a refresh button.

origin.said: "We're gonna build a UI asset designer, which will create assets with their manifest and their identifier. It's going to create separate plugins for the app menu designer, the nav menu designer, the toolbar designer, the banner designer, the embedded widget designer, the widget designer. These are not dependent on the designer, but the designer interface will inherit those other designers. The UI designer plugin will have add-ons, each with their own settings interface and the designer's interface." "Redo them all from scratch." "Make it a build and get the Fable stuff going. Make it super powerful: full-blown context menu, drag and drop, map-based. Every UI asset will also have a context menu section which gives you a preview of the UI, and informs you in multiple ways (tooltips etc)."

origin.said:
# Icon Browser + Icon Manager (Brett, voice)

## 1. Icon Browser plugin
- Ship a starter library: download a couple thousand icons (open-licensed sets), stored as assets.
- Views: tree, grid, list, etc. Categorized, sortable, filterable, searchable. Tree thumbnails toggle on/off.
- Sources (configurable, any type): FTP/SFTP (credentials + root folder), MCP, REST API, HTTP/online, local folder, Google Drive folder, Google Photos album, Dropbox, etc. Per-type config form: credentials when needed, root/path, auth. 'Online' shows a big list of known icon repositories, each with a section for what's needed to access it (API key etc.). Secrets in the secure store.
- Packs: create icon packs by drag and drop between panes. Panes are collapsible and floatable.
- Tab groups: open one or many selected icons into a floating tab group, a docked tab group, or a pane. 'Open new tab group' spawns docked or floating; with a selection it holds those icons, empty it shows a + to add. Drag icons from tree to groups and group to group.
- Save a pack as an icon-pack asset.

## 2. Icon Manager
- Every UI and plugin gets an icon map (icon slots/tags -> icon). All of AmberX, Console, axHub, everything.
- List/grid of every UI with an icon map, filterable by app. Open a map, or open a live preview of the UI and drag icons onto the preview. Save / Apply makes it permanent for that icon tag.
- Global icon pack asset listing every icon in the whole system.
- Inheritance: assign a pack to the whole app (root), or per UI, or per plugin. The child overrides the parent.
- Save changes as a new pack: root/global pack, or a UI/plugin-scoped pack.
- Icon packs are separate from design/style packs. A design pack MAY reference an icon pack but does not have to.
- Switch packs globally; a randomize button reshuffles the whole icon set; generate cohesive packs that follow one theme/style.

## Rules
- Everything is registry assets, with API/MCP/CLI parity and voice control.
- Settings in categorized collapsible sections.
- Submit UI options to UI Review first (at least 3).

steps.text: Contracts: icon-map@1 (slots -> icon refs, scope app | ui | plugin, extends, inheritance child over parent) and icon-source@1 (kind, config, secretRef) asset types in asset-types.json; iconmap-rules.mjs + .d.mts (normalize, errors, ref parsing name | pack:<id>/<glyph>, resolve chain, randomize, cohesive generation), engine iconmap.ts exported from core; fixture spec/fixtures/icon-map.json + check-icon-map.mts; starter assets; validate --framework and schemas green; Kotlin twin recorded as deferred in PORTING.md
steps.why: new shared asset types + cross-port contract

steps.text: Icon library: framework/cli/icon-import.mjs (SVG -> icon-pack glyphs: path, circle, ellipse, rect, line, polyline, polygon; 24 grid; <= 600 glyphs per pack, sets split by category) downloads open-licensed sets (Lucide ISC, Tabler MIT, Feather MIT, Heroicons MIT, Bootstrap Icons MIT, Phosphor MIT) from npm into framework/icon-library/ (icon-library@1 index.json: sets -> packs, licence, counts, categories, tags), every pack a valid icon-pack@1; `icon-import.mjs library --check` (valid, in sync, size budget) wired into CI
steps.why: library format + converter correctness is a contract every port reads

steps.text: Runtime: rt.iconFor(name, scope) resolves through the icon maps (plugin / UI map -> app root map -> active icon pack -> framework glyph), React IconScope context, Icon.tsx reads it; settings keys axf.icons.* (map picks per scope, slot overrides) count as appearance settings so the hub look carries them to every app; actions icons.set | icons.apply | icons.pack | icons.randomize | icons.generate | icons.reset registered for voice / MCP / CLI; check-icon-map covers the runtime path
steps.why: cross-app GUI behaviour in the runtime + appearance contract

steps.text: Icon Browser plugin core (apps/console-web/plugins/icon-browser): plugin.json (lifecycle, commands block, help.json, builtWith), server part (library index + search from framework/icon-library, sources CRUD, private secret store in the data dir, packs save as icon-pack assets, maps list), web: page head, tree / grid / list views with categories, sort, filter, search, thumbnails toggle, virtualised grid; menu.ts entries; settings tab in categorized collapsible sections
steps.why: first consumer of the icon-library and icon-map contracts; shapes the plugin's data model

steps.text: Panes, packs and tab groups: collapsible / floatable panes (library, pack composer, details) on the dock engine; drag icons between panes to compose a pack; Save pack as an icon-pack asset (server writes it, runtime registers it); open one or many selected icons into a docked or floating tab group or a pane through WindowManager (openGroup / openFloating / addTab); 'Open new tab group' docked or floating, empty shows a + to add; drag tree -> group and group -> group
steps.why: changes how GUIs work across apps (window / dock engine use, drag-drop between hosts)

steps.text: Icon Manager page: list / grid of every UI with an icon map (console, plugins, axHub web, AmberX, Molly), filterable by app; map editor (slot -> icon, drops from the browser); live preview of the UI with drops onto its icons; Save / Apply makes the pick permanent for that slot; inheritance view (root -> UI -> plugin, child overrides); assign a pack at root, UI or plugin; Save changes as a new root / scoped pack; global 'every icon' pack; switch packs globally; Randomize; Generate cohesive pack (one set / style)
steps.why: cross-app GUI behaviour: icon maps for every app

steps.text: Sources: per-type config forms (local folder, HTTP, REST, MCP, FTP / SFTP, Google Drive, Google Photos, Dropbox, online repository) with credentials, root / path and auth; secrets saved to the plugin's private store by reference only; framework/schemas/icon-repos.json: the known online icon repositories with what each needs (API key, token, none) shown per repository; test connection; import from a source into the library
steps.why: forms and integrations on top of the contracts

steps.text: Icon maps for every app: framework/cli/icon-map.mjs scan | list | check scans the icon names each UI and plugin uses (console, plugins, axHub web, AmberX, Molly) and writes / updates their icon-map assets; CI check that no UI is without a map; MCP / CLI parity of the plugin commands checked (plugin-commands.mjs check)
Polish: help.json for every control, menu-reach, help-coverage, check-theme / check-controls / check-chrome-assets / plugin-lifecycle / plugin-pages green; settings sections finished; console re-bake

origin.said:
# Icon Browser + Icon Manager (Brett, voice)

## 1. Icon Browser plugin
- Ship a starter library: download a couple thousand icons (open-licensed sets), stored as assets.
- Views: tree, grid, list, etc. Categorized, sortable, filterable, searchable. Tree thumbnails toggle on/off.
- Sources (configurable, any type): FTP/SFTP (credentials + root folder), MCP, REST API, HTTP/online, local folder, Google Drive folder, Google Photos album, Dropbox, etc. Per-type config form: credentials when needed, root/path, auth. 'Online' shows a big list of known icon repositories, each with a section for what's needed to access it (API key etc.). Secrets in the secure store.
- Packs: create icon packs by drag and drop between panes. Panes are collapsible and floatable.
- Tab groups: open one or many selected icons into a floating tab group, a docked tab group, or a pane. 'Open new tab group' spawns docked or floating; with a selection it holds those icons, empty it shows a + to add. Drag icons from tree to groups and group to group.
- Save a pack as an icon-pack asset.

## 2. Icon Manager
- Every UI and plugin gets an icon map (icon slots/tags -> icon). All of AmberX, Console, axHub, everything.
- List/grid of every UI with an icon map, filterable by app. Open a map, or open a live preview of the UI and drag icons onto the preview. Save / Apply makes it permanent for that icon tag.
- Global icon pack asset listing every icon in the whole system.
- Inheritance: assign a pack to the whole app (root), or per UI, or per plugin. The child overrides the parent.
- Save changes as a new pack: root/global pack, or a UI/plugin-scoped pack.
- Icon packs are separate from design/style packs. A design pack MAY reference an icon pack but does not have to.
- Switch packs globally; a randomize button reshuffles the whole icon set; generate cohesive packs that follow one theme/style.

## Rules
- Everything is registry assets, with API/MCP/CLI parity and voice control.
- Settings in categorized collapsible sections.
- Submit UI options to UI Review first (at least 3).

steps.why: cross-app GUI behaviour in the runtime + appearance contract

steps.text: Icon Browser plugin core (apps/console-web/plugins/icon-browser): plugin.json (lifecycle, commands block, help.json, builtWith), server part (library index + search from framework/icon-library, sources CRUD, private secret store in the data dir, packs save as icon-pack assets, maps list), web: page head, tree / grid / list views with categories, sort, filter, search, thumbnails toggle, virtualised grid; menu.ts entries; settings tab in categorized collapsible sections

steps.why: cross-app GUI behaviour: icon maps for every app

before.detail: Fable phase: designer@1 contracts (add-on model, designer + embed asset types, designed@1 manifest + identifier + registration, designer-doc@1 interaction contract, asset-context@1 section), fixtures, validators, checks, PORTING.md, DESIGNER.md. Opus phase: the host plugin, six standalone add-on plugins, voice + API/MCP/CLI, tests, UI Review. Plan Studio: Proposed > Assets (proposed-fzf3). Supersedes the menu / toolbar editors of the old asset-designer pending build.

origin.said: "We're gonna build a UI asset designer, which will create assets with their manifest and their identifier. It's going to create separate plugins for the app menu designer, the nav menu designer, the toolbar designer, the banner designer, the embedded widget designer, the widget designer. These are not dependent on the designer, but the designer interface will inherit those other designers. The UI designer plugin will have add-ons, each with their own settings interface and the designer's interface." "Redo them all from scratch." "Make it a build and get the Fable stuff going. Make it super powerful: full-blown context menu, drag and drop, map-based. Every UI asset will also have a context menu section which gives you a preview of the UI, and informs you in multiple ways (tooltips etc)."

steps.text: designer@1 contract: host + add-on model (designer-addon@1: id, asset types, designer UI view, settings interface asset, designer interface asset, manifest fields, capabilities, drops, voice), the designer asset type (the designer's interface with inherit@1 copies per add-on), rules file + .d.mts, exported from core

Asset output contract: designed@1 manifest + stable identifier (uid, ref, revision, hash, origin), registration as a ui-registry@1 item (coordinated with ui-registry-shortcuts, no duplicate engine) and in the designer library index (designer-library@1, paths per output target); the embed asset type (embed-asset@1)

Interaction contract for every designer (designer-doc@1): one document model with families per asset type (toolbar, banner, nav, app menu, context menu, flat) and asset round trips, ops, multi-select, map canvas (snap, align, distribute, auto layout, zoom), drag-and-drop (parseDrop / canDrop / applyDrop), undo / redo with coalescing, the designer context menu + keyboard map

asset-context@1: the context-menu section every UI asset gets (identity with tooltip, live Preview entry, About, Help, Edit in its designer, Copy id, Where used) and assetInfo in every mode (tooltip, hover card, side panel, help text, say); MenuEntry gains tip / preview / disabled; data-axf-asset attribute contract

Fixtures + validators + checks: spec/fixtures/designer.json replayed by spec/check-designer.mjs (CI), both validators agree, starters (designer ×7, settings ×7, embed ×3), JSON Schemas, re-bake + shared-assets bake, PORTING.md row, DESIGNER.md spec, report, Opus steps written into the plan
PR into the merge queue (never landed directly), THREADS.md + STATUS.md + decisions.md, build linked (builds-live.mjs link)

Host plugin skeleton: plugins/ui-asset-designer from _template (id ai.amberx.axf.console.ui-asset-designer, uiEditor builder, lifecycle, install/uninstall, provides service:axf.designer@1), nav Plugins → UI asset designer, Settings → Plugins sub-tab rendered through settings/designer; plugin-lifecycle check passes

Host server (FastAPI): capability axf.designer@1 (addons, library, get, validate, save, register, preview), designer-library@1 index in the lifecycle dataDir, saves through makeDesigned / withDesigned, built-in ids refused, plugin-commands@1 auto routes; test.py

Host web shell: add-on list (designerAddonChoices, installed / missing with a link to the plugin), asset library panel (designed + built-in per type, search, New / Open / Duplicate / Delete), designer interface + settings interface pickers (inherit@1 copies, Reset to default)

Shared designer shell: map canvas (free / flow / both, grid, snap, rulers, guides, zoom) + layers tree on designerDoc with multi-select (click / ctrl / shift / marquee), drag within the tree and the map, panels placed by the designer interface (left / right / bottom / float / hidden)

Shared inspector from nodeProps (text, icon picker, action picker from rt.actions, view picker from the UI registry, bindings, choices, numbers) + root data fields from asset-types.json; the chrome settings dialog pattern for the designer interface (Settings…)

Shared context menu + keyboard: designerContextMenu entries (tip tooltips, disabled, submenus) on right-click / long-press of nodes and the canvas, DESIGNER_KEYS handling, clipboard (cut / copy / paste within and across designers), undo / redo on createHistory / commit with coalescing from the interface

Shared drag-and-drop in and out: parseDrop / canDrop / applyDrop for palette items, assets from the library, actions, grid hooks (grid-hook@1), embeds, text, URLs and files; drop indicators (before / after / inside, map position); nodeDragPayload for dragging nodes out to other designers

Shared live preview: docked / floating / inline per the interface, desktop + phone frames, live or on-save refresh, through rt.swap on a preview id per type (never the app's real slot); AssetPreview miniature for the asset library cards

Save / publish flow: id suggestion + designedIdErrors, makeDesigned (origin = what Brett said when voice-started), version bump per the interface, library upsert, ui-registry.json declaration of the host (designedRegistryItem) + `ui-registry.mjs generate`, output target app / framework / hub, autosave

asset-context@1 in the runtime: contextExtras '*:asset' from data-axf-asset on every chrome, widget, dialog and embed element (Chrome.tsx, Widgets.tsx, TabGroup.tsx, Overlays.tsx carry the attribute), assetContextSection with the add-on in force, actions asset.preview / asset.about / asset.copyId / asset.usage registered, help@1 entries from assetInfo help-text

Menu rendering of the new entry fields: MenuList / Overlays draw tip (tooltip + Help mode), preview (a live miniature of the asset on hover: AssetPreview in a popover), disabled; About opens the hover card (phone: sheet) and the side panel; Where used lists hosts from the live chrome

App menu designer add-on: works inside the host (registered through the capability) and alone; help.json entries; 3+ preview options (desktop + phone shots) to UI Review (review.mjs submit --kind other --group "ui-asset-designer - <date>")

# Icon Browser + Icon Manager (Brett, voice)

## 1. Icon Browser plugin
- Ship a starter library: download a couple thousand icons (open-licensed sets), stored as assets.
- Views: tree, grid, list, etc. Categorized, sortable, filterable, searchable. Tree thumbnails toggle on/off.
- Sources (configurable, any type): FTP/SFTP (credentials + root folder), MCP, REST API, HTTP/online, local folder, Google Drive folder, Google Photos album, Dropbox, etc. Per-type config form: credentials when needed, root/path, auth. 'Online' shows a big list of known icon repositories, each with a section for what's needed to access it (API key etc.). Secrets in the secure store.
- Packs: create icon packs by drag and drop between panes. Panes are collapsible and floatable.
- Tab groups: open one or many selected icons into a floating tab group, a docked tab group, or a pane. 'Open new tab group' spawns docked or floating; with a selection it holds those icons, empty it shows a + to add. Drag icons from tree to groups and group to group.
- Save a pack as an icon-pack asset.

## 2. Icon Manager
- Every UI and plugin gets an icon map (icon slots/tags -> icon). All of AmberX, Console, axHub, everything.
- List/grid of every UI with an icon map, filterable by app. Open a map, or open a live preview of the UI and drag icons onto the preview. Save / Apply makes it permanent for that icon tag.
- Global icon pack asset listing every icon in the whole system.
- Inheritance: assign a pack to the whole app (root), or per UI, or per plugin. The child overrides the parent.
- Save changes as a new pack: root/global pack, or a UI/plugin-scoped pack.
- Icon packs are separate from design/style packs. A design pack MAY reference an icon pack but does not have to.
- Switch packs globally; a randomize button reshuffles the whole icon set; generate cohesive packs that follow one theme/style.

## Rules
- Everything is registry assets, with API/MCP/CLI parity and voice control.
- Settings in categorized collapsible sections.
- Submit UI options to UI Review first (at least 3).

steps.text: Contracts: icon-map@1 (slots -> icon refs, scope app | ui | plugin, extends, inheritance child over parent) and icon-source@1 (kind, config, secretRef) asset types in asset-types.json; iconmap-rules.mjs + .d.mts (normalize, errors, ref parsing name | pack:<id>/<glyph>, resolve chain, randomize, cohesive generation), engine iconmap.ts exported from core; fixture spec/fixtures/icon-map.json + check-icon-map.mts; starter assets; validate --framework and schemas green; Kotlin twin recorded as deferred in PORTING.md
steps.why: new shared asset types + cross-port contract

steps.text: Icon library: framework/cli/icon-import.mjs (SVG -> icon-pack glyphs: path, circle, ellipse, rect, line, polyline, polygon; 24 grid; <= 600 glyphs per pack, sets split by category) downloads open-licensed sets (Lucide ISC, Tabler MIT, Feather MIT, Heroicons MIT, Bootstrap Icons MIT, Phosphor MIT) from npm into framework/icon-library/ (icon-library@1 index.json: sets -> packs, licence, counts, categories, tags), every pack a valid icon-pack@1; `icon-import.mjs library --check` (valid, in sync, size budget) wired into CI
steps.why: library format + converter correctness is a contract every port reads

steps.text: Runtime: rt.iconFor(name, scope) resolves through the icon maps (plugin / UI map -> app root map -> active icon pack -> framework glyph), React IconScope context, Icon.tsx reads it; settings keys axf.icons.* (map picks per scope, slot overrides) count as appearance settings so the hub look carries them to every app; actions icons.set | icons.apply | icons.pack | icons.randomize | icons.generate | icons.reset registered for voice / MCP / CLI; check-icon-map covers the runtime path
steps.why: cross-app GUI behaviour in the runtime + appearance contract

steps.text: Icon Browser plugin core (apps/console-web/plugins/icon-browser): plugin.json (lifecycle, commands block, help.json, builtWith), server part (library index + search from framework/icon-library, sources CRUD, private secret store in the data dir, packs save as icon-pack assets, maps list), web: page head, tree / grid / list views with categories, sort, filter, search, thumbnails toggle, virtualised grid; menu.ts entries; settings tab in categorized collapsible sections
steps.why: first consumer of the icon-library and icon-map contracts; shapes the plugin's data model

steps.text: Panes, packs and tab groups: collapsible / floatable panes (library, pack composer, details) on the dock engine; drag icons between panes to compose a pack; Save pack as an icon-pack asset (server writes it, runtime registers it); open one or many selected icons into a docked or floating tab group or a pane through WindowManager (openGroup / openFloating / addTab); 'Open new tab group' docked or floating, empty shows a + to add; drag tree -> group and group -> group
steps.why: changes how GUIs work across apps (window / dock engine use, drag-drop between hosts)

steps.text: Icon Manager page: list / grid of every UI with an icon map (console, plugins, axHub web, AmberX, Molly), filterable by app; map editor (slot -> icon, drops from the browser); live preview of the UI with drops onto its icons; Save / Apply makes the pick permanent for that slot; inheritance view (root -> UI -> plugin, child overrides); assign a pack at root, UI or plugin; Save changes as a new root / scoped pack; global 'every icon' pack; switch packs globally; Randomize; Generate cohesive pack (one set / style)
steps.why: cross-app GUI behaviour: icon maps for every app

steps.text: Sources: per-type config forms (local folder, HTTP, REST, MCP, FTP / SFTP, Google Drive, Google Photos, Dropbox, online repository) with credentials, root / path and auth; secrets saved to the plugin's private store by reference only; framework/schemas/icon-repos.json: the known online icon repositories with what each needs (API key, token, none) shown per repository; test connection; import from a source into the library
steps.why: forms and integrations on top of the contracts

steps.text: Icon maps for every app: framework/cli/icon-map.mjs scan | list | check scans the icon names each UI and plugin uses (console, plugins, axHub web, AmberX, Molly) and writes / updates their icon-map assets; CI check that no UI is without a map; MCP / CLI parity of the plugin commands checked (plugin-commands.mjs check)
Polish: help.json for every control, menu-reach, help-coverage, check-theme / check-controls / check-chrome-assets / plugin-lifecycle / plugin-pages green; settings sections finished; console re-bake
Screenshots (desktop + phone) of at least 3 UI options for the browser and the manager submitted to UI Review; report _claude/builds/reports/icon-browser-manager.md; THREADS.md; PR opened and linked

before.title: skins-asset-types
before.detail: Upgrade skins to style every registry asset type (widgets, icon packs, composites, embeds, text blocks), scoped inheritance, registry-driven coverage + CI check. Brief: /root/axf-builds/skins-asset-types/.brief.md. Was queued directly; orchestrator to assign models.

origin.said: What about skins? How's skins doing? Is skins gonna um, be upgraded since we've we've made um so many more asset types? ... Added into skins.

addenda.said: Upgrade the skins system so it styles EVERY asset type now in the registry, not just the original kinds. Cover the new types: embeddable widget, icon pack, composite assets (button = box + text, nav = container + items), data set bar (search/filter/sort), embed, and every element down to text blocks/labels. Skins apply at any scope: global/app/UI/plugin, with child-overrides-parent inheritance (same model as design/icon packs). A skin is a design pack; it MAY reference an icon pack but doesn't have to. Pull the full asset-type list from the registry dynamically so new types are covered automatically going forward (no hardcoded list); add a CI check that fails if a registered asset type has no skin coverage. Voice + API/MCP/CLI parity. Submit at least 3 UI options to UI Review first.

CI: check-skin-coverage fails on a registered type with no skin coverage; android.yml; rebake; typecheck; checks
Customize targets for every drawn type (widgets, badge, label, text): composite parts box / text / icon / items

origin.brief:
# Build: notifications-control-panel

## Brett said (verbatim)
"You need to have an administration panel. I need to control all the notifications. I need you to build a console control panel to enable and control all possible notifications."

Console plugin: one Notifications control panel.
1. Inventory every notification source in console, AmberX, axHub (banners, alerts, approvals/veto, UI Review, builds, merge queue, CI, health checks, account/limits, Follow Amber, AmberX push). Report the list.
2. One registry (notification types, source, channel). Every sender checks it before sending.
3. Panel: per type on/off, channel (banner, AmberX push, sound, console pop-up), priority, quiet hours, test send; master switch; per app.
4. REST + MCP + CLI so it can be set by voice.
5. Coordinate with running build ui-review-notify-audio (UI Review push to AmberX): register its notification type here, don't rebuild it.
6. Tests, README, screenshots to UI Review, PR to the merge queue. Do NOT land directly. Nothing removed. One session, lean chain.
## Addendum 1 (Brett, voice)
"I need groups with commands with triggers with actions."
- Notification groups (user-made, any types in a group, group on/off).
- Triggers: rules for when a notification fires (event, conditions, thresholds, schedule).
- Actions/commands: buttons on each notification that run a command (approve, open screen, run console command); custom commands per group.
- All editable in the panel and via REST/MCP/CLI.

## Brett said (verbatim)
"Run a follow-up." (for requests that arrived after claude-badge-vps and notifications-control-panel finished)

Base: merge branches claude/claude-badge-vps and claude/notifications-control-panel (both finished, not landed) and build on top. Read their briefs' addenda: /root/axf-builds/claude-badge-vps/.brief.md and /root/axf-builds/notifications-control-panel/.brief.md.

A. Badges (one plugin):
1. Claude, axHub, VPS and AmberX badges in ONE plugin; move existing ones in (old ones can be disabled).
2. Per badge: show/hide, icons only or icon + label, label text, icon per state (ok/warn/error/off), banner order.
3. VPS account usage meter (5-hour + weekly used of total, reset time) in the same plugin; reuse the existing usage-meter widget code.
4. Configurable tap action per badge (drop-down, open screen, run command, toggle, nothing). Usage meter default tap = drop-down of every saved Claude account with credits left, reset times, active marker, status. Plain code, zero tokens, cached + refresh.

B. Notifications panel:
5. Groups (user-made, group on/off), triggers (event, conditions, thresholds, schedule), actions/commands on each notification (approve, open screen, run console command, custom per group). Editable in the panel and via REST/MCP/CLI.

Tests, README, report, screenshots to UI Review, ONE PR to the merge queue that supersedes the two branches. Do NOT land directly. One session, lean chain. Stay out of Gizmo and UI registry code (running builds).
## Addendum 1 (Brett, voice) - notifications architecture
"Everything's gonna go through the console. It needs to exist on the console, and then that sends the thing to AmberX to do the notification. It doesn't live on AmberX. AmberX just processes commands from the console."
- The notifications engine (registry, rules, groups, triggers, actions) lives on the console only.
- AmberX is a dumb delivery end: it receives notification commands from the console (show, sound, open link, action buttons that call back to the console) and nothing else. No notification logic or rules in AmberX; any that exist there get moved to the console.

## Addendum 2 (Brett, voice)
"Can I make it so a notification will be a vibration or an alarm or a certain sound, from the console?"
- Yes: per notification type/group on the console: delivery style = silent / vibrate (pattern) / sound (pick from a list, custom upload) / alarm (full-screen, repeats until dismissed). AmberX executes it (notification channels per style so Android honours it). Test button per type.

## Addendum 3 (Brett, voice) - bring to front
"When something is sent over from the console, AmberX opens it up and brings it to the front of my phone. If I say 'open up the console UI Review and bring this project into focus', it brings that right up to the front."
- Console command -> AmberX: bring AmberX to the foreground on the phone (Android full-screen intent / overlay permission as needed) and open the target directly: a screen, a UI Review group, a specific item scrolled into focus.
- New UI Review items auto-open this way (setting to turn off; notification is the fallback).
- Works by voice through the local assistant / Gizmo: 'open UI Review and focus <project>'.
- Builds on PR #365 (ui-review-notify-audio, truthful wake); merge its branch claude/ui-review-notify-audio first, don't rebuild it. APK change via CI.

before.title: skins-asset-types
before.detail: Upgrade skins to style every registry asset type (widgets, icon packs, composites, embeds, text blocks), scoped inheritance, registry-driven coverage + CI check. Brief: /root/axf-builds/skins-asset-types/.brief.md. Was queued directly; orchestrator to assign models.

origin.said: What about skins? How's skins doing? Is skins gonna um, be upgraded since we've we've made um so many more asset types? ... Added into skins.

addenda.said: Upgrade the skins system so it styles EVERY asset type now in the registry, not just the original kinds. Cover the new types: embeddable widget, icon pack, composite assets (button = box + text, nav = container + items), data set bar (search/filter/sort), embed, and every element down to text blocks/labels. Skins apply at any scope: global/app/UI/plugin, with child-overrides-parent inheritance (same model as design/icon packs). A skin is a design pack; it MAY reference an icon pack but doesn't have to. Pull the full asset-type list from the registry dynamically so new types are covered automatically going forward (no hardcoded list); add a CI check that fails if a registered asset type has no skin coverage. Voice + API/MCP/CLI parity. Submit at least 3 UI options to UI Review first.

steps.text: skin-coverage@1 engine: coverage of every registry type (slot / parts / reference / bundle / none) derived from asset-types.json, scope chain global → app → UI → plugin (child overrides parent), fixtures; registry declarations for the few types with no look
skin@1 extension: parts, iconPack, per-scope skins in app-look@1 + composeLook per scope; validators (TS + build engine), schemas, gen-fixtures
CI: check-skin-coverage fails on a registered type with no skin coverage; android.yml; rebake; typecheck; checks
Customize targets for every drawn type (widgets, badge, label, text): composite parts box / text / icon / items
Runtime + React: scope-aware skins on plugin roots and view roots, parts sheet, icon pack setting
Settings → Appearance: scope picker, Follow global switch, coverage list; 3 UI options to UI Review
CLI / API / MCP / voice parity: skins.mjs scopes + coverage, theme-manager routes, console actions
Docs, PORTING, rules, report, THREADS, PR into the merge queue; close skins s9–s11

origin.brief:
# today: approve/deny axHub approvals inside the Dev Console

Brett's words (voice, Nov 6 2026): "It does pop it up in my approval, but when I click it, it brings me to axHub. I don't want it to bring me to axHub."

## Problem
When an axHub approval (confirm or veto countdown) is waiting, the console pops it up (approvals-banner / approval popup), but tapping it navigates to https://axhub.amberxai.com/auth/admin/approvals/<id>. Brett wants to stay in the console.

## Build
1. In the console's approval popup/banner (and any approval row in the console, incl. phone layout), tapping the approval opens an in-console approval view: title, description, the exact call/command, countdown if veto, and Approve / Deny buttons.
2. Approve / Deny call axHub's approval API server-side from the console (console proxy using its existing axHub auth), never by sending Brett to the axHub site. Show the result in place (approved, denied, ran, failed).
3. No link to the axHub page as the default tap. At most a small secondary "open in axHub" option.
4. Register console actions (e.g. approvals.approve / approvals.deny with id) so they work through console commands too, and make console_show approval:<id> open this in-console view.
5. AmberX phone notifications for approvals should open the console's in-console view, not axHub.

## Rules
Follow CLAUDE.md and _claude/rules/RULES.md. Never print or log secrets/tokens. Tests for approve/deny from the console. Update help/docs, THREADS row, orchestrator entry, report. Don't land; leave it for Brett's go.

Make UI Review have a separate tab under each one for anything that requires a choice. You need to be able to select multiple with priorities. If you select multiple, it will create a separate view for each one you selected, with the first one being default.

Not all asset types can have more than one view; a settings interface may not need more than one. But make every choice, even the ones I don't pick, an asset, stored in that plugin's folder as an asset for the library.
Every UI in the Appearance section will allow you to choose from any of the assets that have been made for it.

Everything comes shipped (all options as assets). For UI Review, for everything sent through it, I need a minimum of three choices. A setting for the default number of choices, and an option to enable a prompt any time something is sent, asking me how many options I want built.

origin.brief:
# today: approve/deny axHub approvals inside the Dev Console

Brett's words (voice, Nov 6 2026): "It does pop it up in my approval, but when I click it, it brings me to axHub. I don't want it to bring me to axHub."

## Problem
When an axHub approval (confirm or veto countdown) is waiting, the console pops it up (approvals-banner / approval popup), but tapping it navigates to https://axhub.amberxai.com/auth/admin/approvals/<id>. Brett wants to stay in the console.

## Build
1. In the console's approval popup/banner (and any approval row in the console, incl. phone layout), tapping the approval opens an in-console approval view: title, description, the exact call/command, countdown if veto, and Approve / Deny buttons.
2. Approve / Deny call axHub's approval API server-side from the console (console proxy using its existing axHub auth), never by sending Brett to the axHub site. Show the result in place (approved, denied, ran, failed).
3. No link to the axHub page as the default tap. At most a small secondary "open in axHub" option.
4. Register console actions (e.g. approvals.approve / approvals.deny with id) so they work through console commands too, and make console_show approval:<id> open this in-console view.
5. AmberX phone notifications for approvals should open the console's in-console view, not axHub.

## Rules
Follow CLAUDE.md and _claude/rules/RULES.md. Never print or log secrets/tokens. Tests for approve/deny from the console. Update help/docs, THREADS row, orchestrator entry, report. Don't land; leave it for Brett's go.

# Build: Headless progress file + lean CLAUDE.md chain
Orchestrator build id: headless-progress-file-lean-claude-md-chain (planner.builds). Follow the CLAUDE.md chain and rules as usual.

Goal: headless sessions never stop to update the console; they write progress to a small file the console reads. Cut tokens spent on the CLAUDE.md chain.

Steps (each ~10 min, commit after each):
1. Define progress file format + location per build (current step, status, last update, notes).
2. Headless runner (deploy/claude-headless.sh etc.): write/update progress file after each step without pausing. Use it yourself in this build from step 2 on.
3. Orchestrator: include progress file in every new build on registration.
4. Console: read progress file on demand and show where the build is.
5. Remove old stop-to-update-console behavior from headless sessions.
6. Audit the CLAUDE.md chain headless sessions load (files, size, tokens per step).
7. Headless: load a slim build brief instead of full chain; pull rules files only when a step needs them.
8. Load chain once per session, not every step; verify.

Tick each step done in the orchestrator as you go. Finish with README/help update, report, PR to merge queue.

# Build: ui-registry-shortcuts

## Brett said (verbatim)
"Let's go with a UI shortcuts plugin. All the UIs need to be in a registry. Every single dialog, pop-up, settings interface, main plugin screen, every UI element has to be an asset. Every single asset in the whole app and all its plugins, from a button to a pop-up to a link to a menu to a menu entry, every thing needs to be an asset. That needs to be visible to the API." "Create a registry so I can open them with my voice."

1. Audit: list what is already an asset (chrome assets, settings-ui@1, tab-group@1, jump-menu@1, control@1 screens/dialogs, voice-command@1) and what isn't. Report the gap. Reuse existing contracts; don't duplicate control@1 or voice-command@1.
2. One UI registry (framework contract): every screen, dialog, pop-up, settings interface, menu, menu entry, button, link across console, AmberX, Molly, axHub web, and every plugin. Stable id, kind, owner app/plugin, label, aliases, how to open it. Plugins declare theirs; a scanner fills gaps; CI check that new UI is registered.
3. API/MCP/CLI: list, search, get, open/show/trigger any registered item.
4. Voice: UI Shortcuts plugin opens any registered item by voice (aliases, fuzzy match), wired to voice-command@1 and Gizmo; user-defined shortcuts.
5. Tests, README, report, screenshots to UI Review, PR to the merge queue. Do NOT land directly.

One session, lean chain. Stay out of Gizmo, badges, notifications code (other builds running).
## Addendum 1 (Brett, voice) - local assistant, no AI
"Without AI, I need an assistant that doesn't need Claude, that just knows my app. I should be able to tell it in plain English like: 'yo, make a notification to do this.'"
- Build a local, zero-token assistant on top of the UI registry + voice-command@1 + control@1: plain-English parsing with a grammar/intent matcher (no LLM), fuzzy matching, slots (names, times, on/off), confirmation for writes.
- It can: open any registered UI, change any setting, run any registered command, create/edit notifications and their style (through the notifications plugin's API), queue items for Claude (Gizmo queue) when the request really needs AI.
- Lives on the console; AmberX and Gizmo send it text/voice. 'What can I say?' lists commands. API/MCP/CLI.

## Addendum 2 (Brett, voice) - local LLM fallback
"Yes, we're gonna do that." (run a small local model through Ollama)
- The local assistant uses a small CPU model through Ollama (e.g. llama3.2:3b or qwen2.5:3b, ~4 GB RAM) ONLY as a fallback when the pattern matcher can't map the sentence: the model picks a command from the UI registry, never free-form actions. Zero Claude tokens.
- Share the Ollama install with the Gizmo rebuild (it installs Ollama + an embedding model for transcript RAG); don't install twice. Setting to turn the model off; memory limit; unload when idle.

origin.brief:
# Build: claude-settings-tabs-veto

## Brett said (verbatim)
"The Claude settings interface is getting pretty big. We need to organize it. Give it multiple views, one of them being tabular. If you have it on the tab view, you can set where you want them to appear and how you want them to appear: on the left, on the right, on the top, and the bottom, whether you want the words or an icon." "The veto and the approve are gonna be their own tab in there. Break it down and put it into tabs."
Also: "You don't need to run the 90-second veto thing unless you are writing stuff to the VPS."

1. Audit Claude settings (plugin claude-settings): list every setting, group them into sensible tabs. Report the breakdown.
2. Views: classic (one page, collapsible sections) and tabbed. Tabbed uses the tab-group@1 asset: tab position left / right / top / bottom, labels as words / icons / both. Settings for the view saved per device. Claude settings stays a settings-interface asset.
3. New tab 'Approvals & veto': per axHub tool (or group) choose allow / veto / confirm, veto hold length (seconds), pass durations; reads go without a hold, only VPS writes and account switches hold by default. Writes to the axHub policy through its API (owner-only). Show the current policy table live.
4. REST/MCP/CLI for the view settings and the policy tab.
5. Tests, README, report, screenshots to UI Review, PR to the merge queue. Do NOT land directly. Overlap check with pending item approvals-no-window-spam-on-approve-veto-only-for-vps-writes-and-account-switc; tick its veto step if covered, note it.

One session, lean chain. Stay out of Gizmo, UI registry, badges/notifications code (other builds).
## Addendum 1 (Brett, voice) - where the veto/approval settings live
"Those settings should not be part of the Claude plugin. They can be accessed by any MCP server, the API or the CLI. They can be in Claude settings, they can be in framework settings."
- The approvals/veto policy settings are their own framework-level settings asset (settings-ui@1), owned by the framework, not the claude-settings plugin. Store: framework settings. Exposed on REST + MCP + CLI.
- Mounted in two places as the same asset: Framework settings and a tab in Claude settings. One source of truth.

## Addendum 2 (Brett, voice) - predicted options first
"Give me a bunch of options in UI Review to pick from, like ten."
- BEFORE building the UI: submit 10 predicted screenshots (ui-review-predicted) of where/how Framework settings and the Approvals & veto settings sit in the main settings interface: e.g. own top-level Framework tab; a section inside General; a left-rail group; a settings home card; a gear in the banner; icon tabs top/left/right/bottom variants; a compact phone layout; a two-pane layout. Phone + desktop each.
- Wait for Brett's pick in UI Review, then build that one. The 10 are mockups only, no code written for the losers.

origin.brief:
# claude-accounts-edit: Edit button per account that reruns the wizard

(r2: r1 died at launch, account-2 OAuth expired.)

Brett's words (voice, Nov 6 2026): "Where it lists the accounts, I need to have an edit button next to the switch buttons... that runs the wizard again."

## Problem
In the console's Claude accounts list (ai-keys "Manage Claude accounts" view and the claude-accounts screen), each account row only has Switch. When an account's login expires, there is no way to re-log that specific account. The add-account wizard only adds a new one. Also: the wizard's "Save current account" fails with a bare 'VPS command failed, exit 1' when nobody is logged in (claude-account save prints 'nothing to save: log in or pass a token'); show that message in the UI.

## Build
1. Add an **Edit** button on every account row, right next to Switch, in every place the account list is shown.
2. Edit opens the existing add-account wizard bound to that account (pre-filled name/slot). Finishing it replaces that account's login/credentials in place: same slot, no new account. Per-build login copies for that account pick up the new credentials.
3. Show a clear state on rows whose login is expired/invalid (e.g. "Login expired").
4. Wizard: surface the claude-account command's own output on failure instead of only 'exit 1'.
5. Register a console action claude-accounts.edit (account id arg) so it runs through console commands too.

## Rules
Follow CLAUDE.md and _claude/rules/RULES.md. Never print or log secrets/tokens. Tests for the edit path (re-log replaces creds in place, no duplicate). Update help/docs, THREADS row, orchestrator entry, report. Don't land; leave it for Brett's go.

# Build: notes-tasks-calendar

## Brett said (verbatim)
"In the notes, task manager and to-do (one plugin), we're gonna add a calendar where we can set events and schedules. We can set weekly schedules. And it's gonna be hooked up to our Gmail / Google Calendar through axHub's MCP server."

Base: branch claude/notes-tasks-sync (PR #363, shared notes-tasks plugin); merge it first, build on it.
1. Calendar inside the notes-tasks plugin (console + AmberX): day / week / month / agenda views; events (time, location, notes, reminders); recurring + weekly schedules; tasks with due dates show on it.
2. Two-way sync with Google Calendar through axHub's Google service (build axhub-google, queued). Until that lands, local calendar works on its own; sync switches on when the service exists.
3. Reminders go through the console notifications engine (AmberX only delivers).
4. REST/MCP/CLI + voice commands (UI registry).
5. Tests, README, screenshots to UI Review, PR to the merge queue. Do NOT land directly.

One session, lean chain.
## Addendum 1 (Brett, voice)
"I need a really sweet interface for the scheduling stuff, the schedules. Make it sick."
- Polished, modern calendar UI (framework tokens + theme only): smooth view transitions, drag to create / move / resize events, colour-coded calendars, now-line, mini-month, quick-add bar (plain English: 'gym every Mon Wed 6pm'), weekly schedule editor with drag blocks, phone gestures (swipe days/weeks, long-press drag), dark/light. Phone-first, desktop great too.
- Screenshots of every view (phone + desktop) to UI Review.

## Addendum 2 (Brett, voice)
"Open that in its own window with multiple layouts. Open numerous schedules, days and weeks: a week here and a month there, and drag events from here to there. Attach an RSVP list / invite list to an event with a check mark of who's replied. Send automatic emails to RSVP people, or emails asking people to confirm they've read/seen it. It needs to update in the scheduler on AmberX."
- Calendar opens in its own window (windows@1 / dock@1); multiple panes side by side, each any view/date/calendar; save named layouts; drag events between panes.
- Invite / RSVP list per event: guests, status (invited / yes / no / maybe / seen), check marks, counts. Emails sent through axHub Google (Gmail) when it exists: invites, automatic RSVP reminders, read/seen confirmation requests (tracked link). Replies update the event status live on console and AmberX. Sending email = confirm approval (axHub policy).

## Addendum 3 (Brett, voice)
"Any replies to the emails get logged. They type their reply in a text field that's sent in the email; they have to reply in the text field so it gets logged in the system."
- Each invite/reminder email has a link to a small public reply page (per-guest signed token, no login): RSVP buttons + a text field. Submissions are logged on the event (who, when, answer, message) and update status live on console + AmberX.
- Plain email replies are also caught via Gmail (axHub) and logged on the event when possible, but the reply page is the main path.
- Reply page is rate-limited, token expires, no other data exposed.

before.title: UI asset designer: host plugin + designer add-ons (app menu, nav menu, toolbar, banner, embed, widget), designed@1 manifests, asset context section
before.detail: Fable phase: designer@1 contracts (add-on model, designer + embed asset types, designed@1 manifest + identifier + registration, designer-doc@1 interaction contract, asset-context@1 section), fixtures, validators, checks, PORTING.md, DESIGNER.md. Opus phase: the host plugin, six standalone add-on plugins, voice + API/MCP/CLI, tests, UI Review. Plan Studio: Proposed > Assets (proposed-fzf3). Supersedes the menu / toolbar editors of the old asset-designer pending build.

origin.said: "We're gonna build a UI asset designer, which will create assets with their manifest and their identifier. It's going to create separate plugins for the app menu designer, the nav menu designer, the toolbar designer, the banner designer, the embedded widget designer, the widget designer. These are not dependent on the designer, but the designer interface will inherit those other designers. The UI designer plugin will have add-ons, each with their own settings interface and the designer's interface." "Redo them all from scratch." "Make it a build and get the Fable stuff going. Make it super powerful: full-blown context menu, drag and drop, map-based. Every UI asset will also have a context menu section which gives you a preview of the UI, and informs you in multiple ways (tooltips etc)."

steps.text: designer@1 contract: host + add-on model (designer-addon@1: id, asset types, designer UI view, settings interface asset, designer interface asset, manifest fields, capabilities, drops, voice), the designer asset type (the designer's interface with inherit@1 copies per add-on), rules file + .d.mts, exported from core

Asset output contract: designed@1 manifest + stable identifier (uid, ref, revision, hash, origin), registration as a ui-registry@1 item (coordinated with ui-registry-shortcuts, no duplicate engine) and in the designer library index (designer-library@1, paths per output target); the embed asset type (embed-asset@1)

Interaction contract for every designer (designer-doc@1): one document model with families per asset type (toolbar, banner, nav, app menu, context menu, flat) and asset round trips, ops, multi-select, map canvas (snap, align, distribute, auto layout, zoom), drag-and-drop (parseDrop / canDrop / applyDrop), undo / redo with coalescing, the designer context menu + keyboard map

asset-context@1: the context-menu section every UI asset gets (identity with tooltip, live Preview entry, About, Help, Edit in its designer, Copy id, Where used) and assetInfo in every mode (tooltip, hover card, side panel, help text, say); MenuEntry gains tip / preview / disabled; data-axf-asset attribute contract

Fixtures + validators + checks: spec/fixtures/designer.json replayed by spec/check-designer.mjs (CI), both validators agree, starters (designer ×7, settings ×7, embed ×3), JSON Schemas, re-bake + shared-assets bake, PORTING.md row, DESIGNER.md spec, report, Opus steps written into the plan
PR into the merge queue (never landed directly), THREADS.md + STATUS.md + decisions.md, build linked (builds-live.mjs link)

Host plugin skeleton: plugins/ui-asset-designer from _template (id ai.amberx.axf.console.ui-asset-designer, uiEditor builder, lifecycle, install/uninstall, provides service:axf.designer@1), nav Plugins → UI asset designer, Settings → Plugins sub-tab rendered through settings/designer; plugin-lifecycle check passes

Host server (FastAPI): capability axf.designer@1 (addons, library, get, validate, save, register, preview), designer-library@1 index in the lifecycle dataDir, saves through makeDesigned / withDesigned, built-in ids refused, plugin-commands@1 auto routes; test.py

Host web shell: add-on list (designerAddonChoices, installed / missing with a link to the plugin), asset library panel (designed + built-in per type, search, New / Open / Duplicate / Delete), designer interface + settings interface pickers (inherit@1 copies, Reset to default)

Shared designer shell: map canvas (free / flow / both, grid, snap, rulers, guides, zoom) + layers tree on designerDoc with multi-select (click / ctrl / shift / marquee), drag within the tree and the map, panels placed by the designer interface (left / right / bottom / float / hidden)

Shared inspector from nodeProps (text, icon picker, action picker from rt.actions, view picker from the UI registry, bindings, choices, numbers) + root data fields from asset-types.json; the chrome settings dialog pattern for the designer interface (Settings…)

Shared context menu + keyboard: designerContextMenu entries (tip tooltips, disabled, submenus) on right-click / long-press of nodes and the canvas, DESIGNER_KEYS handling, clipboard (cut / copy / paste within and across designers), undo / redo on createHistory / commit with coalescing from the interface

Shared drag-and-drop in and out: parseDrop / canDrop / applyDrop for palette items, assets from the library, actions, grid hooks (grid-hook@1), embeds, text, URLs and files; drop indicators (before / after / inside, map position); nodeDragPayload for dragging nodes out to other designers

origin.said: What about skins? How's skins doing? Is skins gonna um, be upgraded since we've we've made um so many more asset types? ... Added into skins.

addenda.said: Upgrade the skins system so it styles EVERY asset type now in the registry, not just the original kinds. Cover the new types: embeddable widget, icon pack, composite assets (button = box + text, nav = container + items), data set bar (search/filter/sort), embed, and every element down to text blocks/labels. Skins apply at any scope: global/app/UI/plugin, with child-overrides-parent inheritance (same model as design/icon packs). A skin is a design pack; it MAY reference an icon pack but doesn't have to. Pull the full asset-type list from the registry dynamically so new types are covered automatically going forward (no hardcoded list); add a CI check that fails if a registered asset type has no skin coverage. Voice + API/MCP/CLI parity. Submit at least 3 UI options to UI Review first.

before.detail: The Dev Console keeps disconnecting from Follow Amber: console_follow shows clients 0 a few minutes after a refresh, so approval pop-ups and console_show never arrive. Likely the phone browser backgrounding or killing the socket. Make the console's Follow Amber connection survive: auto-reconnect with backoff, heartbeat, reconnect on visibility/focus/online events, resend queued shows and approvals on reconnect, keep-alive where Android allows, and a visible connected/disconnected indicator. Also: when no console is connected, deliver approvals through AmberX push so they still pop up. Find the root cause first. Orchestrator assigns models.

before.title: UI asset designer: host plugin + designer add-ons (app menu, nav menu, toolbar, banner, embed, widget), designed@1 manifests, asset context section
before.detail: Fable phase: designer@1 contracts (add-on model, designer + embed asset types, designed@1 manifest + identifier + registration, designer-doc@1 interaction contract, asset-context@1 section), fixtures, validators, checks, PORTING.md, DESIGNER.md. Opus phase: the host plugin, six standalone add-on plugins, voice + API/MCP/CLI, tests, UI Review. Plan Studio: Proposed > Assets (proposed-fzf3). Supersedes the menu / toolbar editors of the old asset-designer pending build.

origin.said: "We're gonna build a UI asset designer, which will create assets with their manifest and their identifier. It's going to create separate plugins for the app menu designer, the nav menu designer, the toolbar designer, the banner designer, the embedded widget designer, the widget designer. These are not dependent on the designer, but the designer interface will inherit those other designers. The UI designer plugin will have add-ons, each with their own settings interface and the designer's interface." "Redo them all from scratch." "Make it a build and get the Fable stuff going. Make it super powerful: full-blown context menu, drag and drop, map-based. Every UI asset will also have a context menu section which gives you a preview of the UI, and informs you in multiple ways (tooltips etc)."

steps.text: designer@1 contract: host + add-on model (designer-addon@1: id, asset types, designer UI view, settings interface asset, designer interface asset, manifest fields, capabilities, drops, voice), the designer asset type (the designer's interface with inherit@1 copies per add-on), rules file + .d.mts, exported from core

Asset output contract: designed@1 manifest + stable identifier (uid, ref, revision, hash, origin), registration as a ui-registry@1 item (coordinated with ui-registry-shortcuts, no duplicate engine) and in the designer library index (designer-library@1, paths per output target); the embed asset type (embed-asset@1)

Interaction contract for every designer (designer-doc@1): one document model with families per asset type (toolbar, banner, nav, app menu, context menu, flat) and asset round trips, ops, multi-select, map canvas (snap, align, distribute, auto layout, zoom), drag-and-drop (parseDrop / canDrop / applyDrop), undo / redo with coalescing, the designer context menu + keyboard map

asset-context@1: the context-menu section every UI asset gets (identity with tooltip, live Preview entry, About, Help, Edit in its designer, Copy id, Where used) and assetInfo in every mode (tooltip, hover card, side panel, help text, say); MenuEntry gains tip / preview / disabled; data-axf-asset attribute contract

Fixtures + validators + checks: spec/fixtures/designer.json replayed by spec/check-designer.mjs (CI), both validators agree, starters (designer ×7, settings ×7, embed ×3), JSON Schemas, re-bake + shared-assets bake, PORTING.md row, DESIGNER.md spec, report, Opus steps written into the plan
PR into the merge queue (never landed directly), THREADS.md + STATUS.md + decisions.md, build linked (builds-live.mjs link)

origin.said:
# Icon Browser + Icon Manager (Brett, voice)

## 1. Icon Browser plugin
- Ship a starter library: download a couple thousand icons (open-licensed sets), stored as assets.
- Views: tree, grid, list, etc. Categorized, sortable, filterable, searchable. Tree thumbnails toggle on/off.
- Sources (configurable, any type): FTP/SFTP (credentials + root folder), MCP, REST API, HTTP/online, local folder, Google Drive folder, Google Photos album, Dropbox, etc. Per-type config form: credentials when needed, root/path, auth. 'Online' shows a big list of known icon repositories, each with a section for what's needed to access it (API key etc.). Secrets in the secure store.
- Packs: create icon packs by drag and drop between panes. Panes are collapsible and floatable.
- Tab groups: open one or many selected icons into a floating tab group, a docked tab group, or a pane. 'Open new tab group' spawns docked or floating; with a selection it holds those icons, empty it shows a + to add. Drag icons from tree to groups and group to group.
- Save a pack as an icon-pack asset.

## 2. Icon Manager
- Every UI and plugin gets an icon map (icon slots/tags -> icon). All of AmberX, Console, axHub, everything.
- List/grid of every UI with an icon map, filterable by app. Open a map, or open a live preview of the UI and drag icons onto the preview. Save / Apply makes it permanent for that icon tag.
- Global icon pack asset listing every icon in the whole system.
- Inheritance: assign a pack to the whole app (root), or per UI, or per plugin. The child overrides the parent.
- Save changes as a new pack: root/global pack, or a UI/plugin-scoped pack.
- Icon packs are separate from design/style packs. A design pack MAY reference an icon pack but does not have to.
- Switch packs globally; a randomize button reshuffles the whole icon set; generate cohesive packs that follow one theme/style.

## Rules
- Everything is registry assets, with API/MCP/CLI parity and voice control.
- Settings in categorized collapsible sections.
- Submit UI options to UI Review first (at least 3).

steps.text: Contracts: icon-map@1 (slots -> icon refs, scope app | ui | plugin, extends, inheritance child over parent) and icon-source@1 (kind, config, secretRef) asset types in asset-types.json; iconmap-rules.mjs + .d.mts (normalize, errors, ref parsing name | pack:<id>/<glyph>, resolve chain, randomize, cohesive generation), engine iconmap.ts exported from core; fixture spec/fixtures/icon-map.json + check-icon-map.mts; starter assets; validate --framework and schemas green; Kotlin twin recorded as deferred in PORTING.md

Icon library: framework/cli/icon-import.mjs (SVG -> icon-pack glyphs: path, circle, ellipse, rect, line, polyline, polygon; 24 grid; <= 600 glyphs per pack, sets split by category) downloads open-licensed sets (Lucide ISC, Tabler MIT, Feather MIT, Heroicons MIT, Bootstrap Icons MIT, Phosphor MIT) from npm into framework/icon-library/ (icon-library@1 index.json: sets -> packs, licence, counts, categories, tags), every pack a valid icon-pack@1; `icon-import.mjs library --check` (valid, in sync, size budget) wired into CI

Runtime: rt.iconFor(name, scope) resolves through the icon maps (plugin / UI map -> app root map -> active icon pack -> framework glyph), React IconScope context, Icon.tsx reads it; settings keys axf.icons.* (map picks per scope, slot overrides) count as appearance settings so the hub look carries them to every app; actions icons.set | icons.apply | icons.pack | icons.randomize | icons.generate | icons.reset registered for voice / MCP / CLI; check-icon-map covers the runtime path

Icon Browser plugin core (apps/console-web/plugins/icon-browser): plugin.json (lifecycle, commands block, help.json, builtWith), server part (library index + search from framework/icon-library, sources CRUD, private secret store in the data dir, packs save as icon-pack assets, maps list), web: page head, tree / grid / list views with categories, sort, filter, search, thumbnails toggle, virtualised grid; menu.ts entries; settings tab in categorized collapsible sections

Panes, packs and tab groups: collapsible / floatable panes (library, pack composer, details) on the dock engine; drag icons between panes to compose a pack; Save pack as an icon-pack asset (server writes it, runtime registers it); open one or many selected icons into a docked or floating tab group or a pane through WindowManager (openGroup / openFloating / addTab); 'Open new tab group' docked or floating, empty shows a + to add; drag tree -> group and group -> group

Icon Manager page: list / grid of every UI with an icon map (console, plugins, axHub web, AmberX, Molly), filterable by app; map editor (slot -> icon, drops from the browser); live preview of the UI with drops onto its icons; Save / Apply makes the pick permanent for that slot; inheritance view (root -> UI -> plugin, child overrides); assign a pack at root, UI or plugin; Save changes as a new root / scoped pack; global 'every icon' pack; switch packs globally; Randomize; Generate cohesive pack (one set / style)

Sources: per-type config forms (local folder, HTTP, REST, MCP, FTP / SFTP, Google Drive, Google Photos, Dropbox, online repository) with credentials, root / path and auth; secrets saved to the plugin's private store by reference only; framework/schemas/icon-repos.json: the known online icon repositories with what each needs (API key, token, none) shown per repository; test connection; import from a source into the library

Icon maps for every app: framework/cli/icon-map.mjs scan | list | check scans the icon names each UI and plugin uses (console, plugins, axHub web, AmberX, Molly) and writes / updates their icon-map assets; CI check that no UI is without a map; MCP / CLI parity of the plugin commands checked (plugin-commands.mjs check)
Polish: help.json for every control, menu-reach, help-coverage, check-theme / check-controls / check-chrome-assets / plugin-lifecycle / plugin-pages green; settings sections finished; console re-bake
Screenshots (desktop + phone) of at least 3 UI options for the browser and the manager submitted to UI Review; report _claude/builds/reports/icon-browser-manager.md; THREADS.md; PR opened and linked

before.title: UI asset designer: host plugin + designer add-ons (app menu, nav menu, toolbar, banner, embed, widget), designed@1 manifests, asset context section
before.detail: Fable phase: designer@1 contracts (add-on model, designer + embed asset types, designed@1 manifest + identifier + registration, designer-doc@1 interaction contract, asset-context@1 section), fixtures, validators, checks, PORTING.md, DESIGNER.md. Opus phase: the host plugin, six standalone add-on plugins, voice + API/MCP/CLI, tests, UI Review. Plan Studio: Proposed > Assets (proposed-fzf3). Supersedes the menu / toolbar editors of the old asset-designer pending build.

origin.said: "We're gonna build a UI asset designer, which will create assets with their manifest and their identifier. It's going to create separate plugins for the app menu designer, the nav menu designer, the toolbar designer, the banner designer, the embedded widget designer, the widget designer. These are not dependent on the designer, but the designer interface will inherit those other designers. The UI designer plugin will have add-ons, each with their own settings interface and the designer's interface." "Redo them all from scratch." "Make it a build and get the Fable stuff going. Make it super powerful: full-blown context menu, drag and drop, map-based. Every UI asset will also have a context menu section which gives you a preview of the UI, and informs you in multiple ways (tooltips etc)."

steps.text: designer@1 contract: host + add-on model (designer-addon@1: id, asset types, designer UI view, settings interface asset, designer interface asset, manifest fields, capabilities, drops, voice), the designer asset type (the designer's interface with inherit@1 copies per add-on), rules file + .d.mts, exported from core

Asset output contract: designed@1 manifest + stable identifier (uid, ref, revision, hash, origin), registration as a ui-registry@1 item (coordinated with ui-registry-shortcuts, no duplicate engine) and in the designer library index (designer-library@1, paths per output target); the embed asset type (embed-asset@1)

Interaction contract for every designer (designer-doc@1): one document model with families per asset type (toolbar, banner, nav, app menu, context menu, flat) and asset round trips, ops, multi-select, map canvas (snap, align, distribute, auto layout, zoom), drag-and-drop (parseDrop / canDrop / applyDrop), undo / redo with coalescing, the designer context menu + keyboard map

asset-context@1: the context-menu section every UI asset gets (identity with tooltip, live Preview entry, About, Help, Edit in its designer, Copy id, Where used) and assetInfo in every mode (tooltip, hover card, side panel, help text, say); MenuEntry gains tip / preview / disabled; data-axf-asset attribute contract

Fixtures + validators + checks: spec/fixtures/designer.json replayed by spec/check-designer.mjs (CI), both validators agree, starters (designer ×7, settings ×7, embed ×3), JSON Schemas, re-bake + shared-assets bake, PORTING.md row, DESIGNER.md spec, report, Opus steps written into the plan
PR into the merge queue (never landed directly), THREADS.md + STATUS.md + decisions.md, build linked (builds-live.mjs link)

Host plugin skeleton: plugins/ui-asset-designer from _template (id ai.amberx.axf.console.ui-asset-designer, uiEditor builder, lifecycle, install/uninstall, provides service:axf.designer@1), nav Plugins → UI asset designer, Settings → Plugins sub-tab rendered through settings/designer; plugin-lifecycle check passes

Host server (FastAPI): capability axf.designer@1 (addons, library, get, validate, save, register, preview), designer-library@1 index in the lifecycle dataDir, saves through makeDesigned / withDesigned, built-in ids refused, plugin-commands@1 auto routes; test.py

Host web shell: add-on list (designerAddonChoices, installed / missing with a link to the plugin), asset library panel (designed + built-in per type, search, New / Open / Duplicate / Delete), designer interface + settings interface pickers (inherit@1 copies, Reset to default)

Shared designer shell: map canvas (free / flow / both, grid, snap, rulers, guides, zoom) + layers tree on designerDoc with multi-select (click / ctrl / shift / marquee), drag within the tree and the map, panels placed by the designer interface (left / right / bottom / float / hidden)

Shared inspector from nodeProps (text, icon picker, action picker from rt.actions, view picker from the UI registry, bindings, choices, numbers) + root data fields from asset-types.json; the chrome settings dialog pattern for the designer interface (Settings…)

Shared context menu + keyboard: designerContextMenu entries (tip tooltips, disabled, submenus) on right-click / long-press of nodes and the canvas, DESIGNER_KEYS handling, clipboard (cut / copy / paste within and across designers), undo / redo on createHistory / commit with coalescing from the interface

Shared drag-and-drop in and out: parseDrop / canDrop / applyDrop for palette items, assets from the library, actions, grid hooks (grid-hook@1), embeds, text, URLs and files; drop indicators (before / after / inside, map position); nodeDragPayload for dragging nodes out to other designers

Shared live preview: docked / floating / inline per the interface, desktop + phone frames, live or on-save refresh, through rt.swap on a preview id per type (never the app's real slot); AssetPreview miniature for the asset library cards

Save / publish flow: id suggestion + designedIdErrors, makeDesigned (origin = what Brett said when voice-started), version bump per the interface, library upsert, ui-registry.json declaration of the host (designedRegistryItem) + `ui-registry.mjs generate`, output target app / framework / hub, autosave

asset-context@1 in the runtime: contextExtras '*:asset' from data-axf-asset on every chrome, widget, dialog and embed element (Chrome.tsx, Widgets.tsx, TabGroup.tsx, Overlays.tsx carry the attribute), assetContextSection with the add-on in force, actions asset.preview / asset.about / asset.copyId / asset.usage registered, help@1 entries from assetInfo help-text

Menu rendering of the new entry fields: MenuList / Overlays draw tip (tooltip + Help mode), preview (a live miniature of the asset on hover: AssetPreview in a popover), disabled; About opens the hover card (phone: sheet) and the side panel; Where used lists hosts from the live chrome

App menu designer add-on: plugin skeleton from plugins/_template (id ai.amberx.axf.console.app-menu-designer, provides service:axf.designer-addon@1 + designer:app-menu, designer.json, lifecycle, install/uninstall, Settings → Plugins sub-tab rendered through settings/designer-app-menu), standalone view app-menu-designer mounting the shared designer shell

App menu designer add-on: editor on designerDoc (menus, items, separators, submenus, live-list providers, badges, check marks, placement) with the shared canvas, tree, inspector (nodeProps), context menu, drag-and-drop and undo; live preview through rt.swap on a preview id

App menu designer add-on: works inside the host (registered through the capability) and alone; help.json entries; 3+ preview options (desktop + phone shots) to UI Review (review.mjs submit --kind other --group "ui-asset-designer - <date>")
